• Demonstrate high levels of self-motivation and initiative to effectively problem solve.

Additional Information
About our benefits:
We recognise that our people are at the heart of our business, without them we wouldn’t be able to deliver our award-winning service to millions of customers across the country each day. It’s important to us that we demonstrate our recognition of you in providing you with more than just a salary and job stability. To name but a few…
• Holiday trading
• Enhanced maternity and paternity package
• Free life assurance of 4 x salary on joining the pension scheme
• Free onsite car parking for all employees
• Discounted shopping from 100’s of retailers including up to 5% off supermarket shopping
• Milestone Days off to celebrate with your family and friends
• For employees who regularly use a screen as part of their job we offer free eye tests and support with the cost of glasses
Joining DPD can lead to not just a stable job but also a career. DPD prides itself on recognising and developing talent alongside a desire to promote from within. As a continually growing and evolving organisation, we are proud to offer a great number of development and promotion opportunities.
If you identify with our aims and values and can help us deliver our customers' promises, then this is the job for you! Apply today.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/frasersgroup/74.description_excerpt:
About This Job
The Role:
As a Supervisor you will be responsible for leading and developing a team of Warehouse Operatives and Trainee Supervisors, driving performance, productivity, and engagement across the shift. Working closely with the Section Manager and wider Warehouse Leadership team, you'll ensure operational targets are achieved, labour is effectively planned, and customer demand is fulfilled on time and in full. You'll champion a strong safety culture, support continuous improvement initiatives, and play a key role in embedding positive cultural change to enhance employee retention and performance.
Key Responsibilities:
• Direct line management and coaching of Warehouse Operatives / Trainee Supervisors including 1:1's to discuss performance vs expectation, identifying SMART goals when performance not met in any of the key functional areas within responsibility
• Working with the Section Manager for your department to monitor delivery to plan and key areas for your shift improve
• Driving performance on key metrics ensuring an efficient warehouse operation which can fulfill customer web and store demand on time and in full
• Driving the highest standards of safety on site, working with the Safety team to ensure adherence to all safety routines/procedures (e.g. Floor Safety Inspections, Hazard Spotting, Safety Gembas, Risk Assessments, Audits)
• Reviewing weekly labour plan to ensure cover is adequate, sharing with Section Manager, highlighting issues/feedback.
• Providing detail when daily/weekly targets are not met and creating plan to bridge
• Alongside the Warehouse Leadership team, you'll partner with other key stakeholders to ensure all strategic activity is on track and supported
• Supporting the successful implementation of culture change and turnover reduction

Qualifications
• Experience in Warehousing, Logistics or Supply Chain
• High potential for people and change management
• Good systems skills
• Customer focused approach to operational management
• Resilient, flexible and approachable
• Problem solving ability in a fast paced business
• You will be working on a rotation shift pattern, 5 days out of 7 including weekends

Additional Information
Along with your benefits package we also offer a wide range of perks for our colleagues:
Frasers Champion- Our employees are at the heart of our business and we ensure individuals are recognised every single month for their hard work. Frasers Champion is a peer nominated scheme where 8 winners will receive double their pay for a month where they have lived the Frasers Group values.
Retail Reconnect – In order to build the planets most admired and compelling brand ecosystem, all employees must understand our business, product and customers. Each financial year, head office employees will gain insights by spending one to two days in one of our stores or the warehouse. The goal is to learn how the work you do impacts our teams on the frontline, and to bring ideas back to the office which will improve how we work.
Fearless 1200 – Fearless 1200 is our way of recognising our growth. It’s bold, ambitious, and designed to reward colleagues across the business for living our values and delivering impact. Fearless 1200 links how we perform to how we're rewarded – check out the video link to find out more - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O0qmvJofMew
Employee Welfare
Frasers Fit – Our Everlast Gyms Team are on a mission to make our workforce the best, and fittest on the planet! We run free gym classes for employees as well as discounted memberships to our clubs. Frasers Fit is our wellbeing programme which aims to support and improve colleagues Physical, Financial & Mental wellbeing. The app is accessible for every employee and includes training, nutrition and lifestyle advice- all completely free.
Retail Trust – We know that its not just about physical health, mental wellness is equally important which is why all of our employees get free access and support from the Retail Trust charity. This includes a 24 hour wellbeing helpline, wellness hub, counselling and financial/legal support.
What’s next?
Our Recruitment Team will be reviewing applications and all candidates will receive a response, whether you are successful or unsuccessful. Shortlisted applicants may be asked to confirm a few key details before being booked in for a first stage interview with the Recruiter - this will be behaviourally focussed and centred around how you align with our Culture and Values. If successful we anticipate one or two further interview stages with the Hiring Manager/wider team which will be more technically focussed and could include a presentation/task so we can see your skills in action.

Lyme Bay Dental & Implant Clinic are looking for a Dental Hygienist to join our award-winning 3 surgery practice working in multi-disciplinary team.

About This Job
As a Kitchen Porter at Potters Resorts Five Lakes, you will play a key role in supporting the kitchen team by ensuring a clean, organized, and efficient kitchen environment. You will assist in food preparation, washing dishes, and maintaining kitchen equipment and utensils, ensuring the highest standards of hygiene and cleanliness are upheld.
Key Responsibilities:
• Clean and sanitize kitchen dishes, utensils, pots, pans, and cooking equipment.
• Ensure all kitchen work areas, including floors and surfaces, are kept clean and hygienic.
• Assist with food preparation tasks, such as chopping vegetables, preparing ingredients, and helping chefs as needed.
• Collect and dispose of kitchen waste in a safe and efficient manner.
• Ensure that all food and equipment are stored properly to maintain health and safety standards.
• Assist with deliveries, ensuring stock is organized and stored appropriately.
• Follow safety procedures and maintain hygiene standards in line with Food Safety regulations.
• Maintain a positive and professional working relationship with colleagues and supervisors.
• Adhere to the company’s health and safety policies and procedures.
Hours:
•
Part-time role, approx 20 - 25 hours per week
•
Straight shifts – no split shifts!
•
Shifts will be either, or a combination of:
•
7:30am – 4:00pm
•
2pm - 10.30
Pay:  Earn between £10.85 and £12.71 per hour, depending on your age
*A UK driving licence and your own vehicle is essential as you will be unable to reach us using public transport.
*This is a permanent position - unfortunately, we are unable to consider students looking for work during their college/university holidays.

Qualifications
• Previous experience in a kitchen environment is advantageous but not essential.
• A good understanding of hygiene and food safety standards.
• Ability to work in a fast-paced environment while maintaining attention to detail.
• A positive and proactive attitude with the ability to work well as part of a team.
• Flexibility to work different shifts, including evenings, weekends, and holidays.
• Good communication skills and ability to follow instructions.
• This is a physically demanding role

Additional Information
As part of our team, we will offer you …
• Free use of Gym and Swimming Pool
• 30% Discount on products in the shop
• Discounted holidays for you and your family at both our Hopton-on-Sea and Five Lakes Resorts
• Free Team Lunch available daily
• An all-year-round position (not seasonal)
• Free Parking
• Cycle to Work Scheme
• Discounted Tickets for you and family or friends to join us for a drinks-all-inclusive ‘Evening of Entertainment’ on Resort
• Free access to our Employee Assistance and Wellbeing Programmes. Including advice and support with health checks, access to GP’s, mental health support and counselling
Potters Resorts is an equal opportunities employer. We will consider all qualified candidates without regard to age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation. Our recruitment team are happy to support with any reasonable adjustments that are needed within the recruitment process.

About This Job
Due to ongoing demand and growth, we are looking for people with kind, compassionate hearts who want to make a true difference to the quality of life for our clients to join our team in Gillingham as a CAREGiver. As a CAREGiver, you will provide a variety of non-medical services to help them keep independent in their own home.
You do not need any experience or particular qualifications to become a CAREGiver. However, it would be useful to have some experience of working in a care setting or interacting with older people. This could be personal experience of caring for a family member or voluntary experience. You will have a passion for supporting others and pride yourself on delivering an outstanding service. You will be reliable, trustworthy and respectful. You will enjoy building professional friendships and comfortable in spending time in the company of others.
Day to day CAREGiver responsibilities can include:
·       Assisting with personal care, helping your client wash and dress.
·       Meal preparation and light house work
·       Accompanying your client to appointments
·       Companionship

Qualifications
Full training provided.

Additional Information
As a CAREGiver, you will receive industry leading training, great rates of pay and excellent support.
If you're looking for work which is extremely rewarding and satisfactory and have a high-degree of  flexibility to meet our clients' needs, we would love to hear from you. Please click on 'I'm Interested' or alternatively, contact us on 01634557070

We are seeking a highly motivated and commercially astute Senior Surveyor / Consultant to join our Hotel Advisory Services team in London. This role will focus on providing strategic hotel advice across feasibility studies, brand and operator selection, development transactions, advisory and asset management support to a diverse portfolio of hotel and hospitality assets. The successful candidate will play a key role in delivering high-quality client service, driving business development, and contributing to the continued growth of the hotel advisory practice.
Key Responsibilities
• Deliver advisory services for hotel, resort, and hospitality assets across the UK and EMEA
• Undertake feasibility studies, market analysis, and highest and best use assessments
• Support and lead on development transactions, including acquisitions, disposals, and operator selection processes
• Prepare detailed financial models, cash flow forecasts, and investment appraisals
• Produce high-quality reports, presentations, and client deliverables
• Build and maintain strong client relationships with investors, owners, operators, and lenders
• Identify and pursue new business opportunities to grow the hotel advisory pipeline
• Collaborate with wider hotel teams across capital markets, agency and valuation
• Mentor junior team members and contribute to team development
Skills & Experience
• Proven experience in hotel advisory or hospitality real estate
• Strong financial modelling and analytical skills
• Good understanding of hotel operations, brands, and management agreements
• Excellent report writing and presentation skills
• Commercially driven with strong business development capability
• Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines effectively
Key Competencies
• Strategic thinking and problem-solving
• Strong interpersonal and communication skills
• Attention to detail and high standards of delivery
• Team-oriented with the ability to work independently
• Client-focused with a proactive approach

• Opportunity to work with a leading global real estate advisor
• Exposure to high-profile hotel and hospitality projects
• Collaborative and entrepreneurial working environment
• Competitive salary and performance-related bonus
• Clear career progression pathways

• Degree in Real Estate, Finance, Hospitality, or a related field
• Strong knowledge of the UK and/or European hotel market
• Right to work in the UK

A great dental nurse can transform a patient’s day. Come and make a difference with us.

• Part-time hours: 22.5 hours per week
• Typical shifts: 7.5 hours per day, worked across Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, between our opening hours of 7:45am–7:00pm, with one Saturday shift per month.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/ingeus1/7440001.description_excerpt:
About This Job
• Starting Salary £51,582
• Full time Monday - Friday 9.00am - 5.00pm
• Opportunity to achieve a £2k salary uplift over the first 12 months, based on achievement of development milestones.
• Further salary uplifts as you learn new specialist skills from year 2.
• Up to 10% quarterly discretionary bonus
• 25 days holiday (+BH) with the option to buy more
Are you looking to your clinical skills in a different way? As a Functional Assessor, you'll continue to utilise your clinical expertise, maintain your registration, and enjoy a better work-life balance. If you have a minimum of 12 months' post-registration experience and have been practising as a clinician throughout the last year, we'd love to hear from you. If you are a pharmacist, we welcome your application if you have a minimum of 18 months experience.
Flexibility and remote working:
We offer a number of flexible working arrangements that suit those who prefer to work in an Assessment Centre full time or in a hybrid role.
Working hours throughout your training are 9.00am -5.00pm Monday to Friday. Once training has been completed (typically around six months), other working patterns are available.
What you’ll be doing as a Functional Assessor:
• Carrying out functional assessments with claimants’ face to face, via video & telephone to assess their ability to undertake activities of daily living.
• Asking focused questions and use active listening and critical reasoning skills to gather accurate information throughout the claimant Assessment.
• Produce high quality, structured clinical reports on all claimants you assess, for submission to the DWP.
• Working alongside other highly experienced clinical colleagues to ensure high-quality & clinically fair assessments for all claimants.
As a Functional Assessor with Ingeus you can expect:
• Predictable hours
• Up to 10% quarterly discretionary bonus
• 25 days holiday (+BH) with the option to buy more
• Private pension
• Private medical insurance
• Maternity and Parental Leave
• Paid training, CPD + reimbursed registration fees
• Paid, structured training to achieve formal DWP accreditation
• A high performing, supportive clinically led culture
• Clear career routes within Ingeus and the wider APM Group
• Online shopping discounts
• Variety of other financial and lifestyle options
• £2000 refer a friend scheme
Whilst you will not be making decisions or recommendations as to the services and benefits for claimants, you will be using your clinical experience to ask the right questions to fully understand the claimants needs and living environment, gathering accurate information for the DWP to make those decisions.
Is this role right for you?
Many clinicians find the role of a Functional Assessor rewarding, but it’s also challenging at the same time and it’s not the right fit for everyone.
This role would suit someone who:
• Thrives on service excellence in a high performing working environment that offers structure and the opportunity to use your clinical skills in a different way.
• Is open to a formalised programme of training to become a DWP approved Functional Assessor.
• Is receptive to ongoing constructive feedback, ensuring our claimants continually get the very best experience.
• Has confidence in their ability to use computers and in learning different software packages to complete detailed, high-quality reports for all claimants assessed.
This role may not be the best match for you if:
• You are not comfortable using or are unfamiliar with technology.
• You dislike writing detailed reports.
• You prefer a more hands on approach to clinical care.
• You’re not looking for a new direction nor a period of retraining into a new role.
• You don’t enjoy working in an environment with targets.
• You are not looking for a role that requires you to work on site for some or all of your working week.3 days a week.
We look forward to receiving your application!

Qualifications
Who We’re Looking For
• NMC-registered Adult Nurses (RGN, RMN, RNLD) or HCPC-registered Physiotherapists, Occupational Therapists and Paramedics or GPHC-registered Pharmacists.
With excellent communication & critical-thinking skills, the ability to type and confidence using computers

Additional Information
At Ingeus, our culture is built on treating everyone with dignity, ensuring every individual feels valued, respected and recognised for their contribution.
As a Disability Confident Employer, we understand that everyone’s journey is different, and we’re committed to making our recruitment process as inclusive and accessible as possible. If you require any support or adjustments—whether that’s help with the application, interview format, or anything else—we’re here to listen and work with you to find the best approach. Our goal is to ensure you can showcase your skills and potential in a way that works for you. Please don’t hesitate to contact us to discuss how we can support you.
Please note, we may shortlist and conduct interviews before the closing date and we may close this role early if we receive enough applications.

About This Job
Utility Surveyor - Aylesford and surrounding areas
Are you an experienced Utility Surveyor looking to advance your career in a dynamic and supportive environment? Based in Aylesford or surrounding areas, we are seeking a skilled professional to join our team, helping deliver accurate and reliable utility mapping and survey services across a variety of projects. This role offers the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology, contribute to critical infrastructure projects, and grow within a company that values precision, safety, and professional development.
The tasks you will undertake will include (but are not limited to):
•    Conducting GPR and Utility Mapping surveys using cutting-edge equipment
•    Undertake investigative utility surveys and conduct paperwork in accordance with company procedures
•    Engage with other site surveyors, contractors, suppliers, clients
•    Create Utility Survey Reports
•    Carry out appropriate quality control checks and issue data to CAD
•    Check all survey drawings before they are issued to our customer
•    Mentor and train Trainee & Junior Surveyors, as required
•    Provide technical support to Project Managers and internal staff members
Travel across the UK is very common. Candidates must be open to working away from home during the week and accommodate night or evening shifts as needed.

Qualifications
To be successful in this role, you will be able to demonstrate:
•    Excellent knowledge and experience of underground utility tracing and GPR
•    Experience working across a wide variety of environments and on complex surveys
•    Ability to post-process GPR data
•    Working knowledge/understanding of PAS 128:2014 specification surveys
•    Ability and willingness to work flexibly
•    A full UK manual driving license
•    CSCS Card
It is desirable, that you also have some or all of the following:
•    Ability to use CAD software
•    Ability to use Microsoft Word
•    ProQual (NVQ) Level 3
•    SSSTS
Salary: £28,598–£45,366 per annum, depending on experience, plus enhanced pay for night shifts and optional weekend working.

Additional Information
Why SOCOTEC?
Join a thriving community of over 2,000 industry professionals who are passionate about making a real difference. At SOCOTEC UK, we're not just delivering services - we're shaping the future of testing, inspection, and certification across the nation.
What sets us apart? Our people. We've built our reputation on attracting exceptional talent like you and empowering them to deliver excellence at every turn. Our comprehensive range of TIC services means you'll have the opportunity to work on diverse, challenging projects that truly matter.
In this role, you won't just be another employee - you'll be a key player in our continued success story. Your expertise will directly contribute to our mission of building a safer, more sustainable world, while you grow your career alongside some of the industry's finest professionals.
Your Career, Your Way
Build a traditional career path or explore opportunities across multiple disciplines - all within SOCOTEC. Your choice, your direction.
Work Your Way
Local, national, or global projects. Office-based, remote, or hybrid. We offer the flexibility that empowers you to perform at your best.
Committed to Your Growth
From day one, you'll have access to comprehensive training, mentorship, and development programs. We support every step of your professional journey. #YouGrowWeGrow
Think you've got what it takes to add value to our success? We would love to hear from you and look forward to receiving your application.
Building a safer and more sustainable world is the core mission we set out to achieve at SOCOTEC, it is at the heart of everything that we do. We are committed to acting as a key player in society, investing in innovative solutions to ensure social and environmental concerns are at the forefront of all of our business operations.

The Head of Architecture & Design, UK & Ireland is a senior leadership position responsible for driving the strategic direction, growth, technical excellence, and market reputation of AECOM’s architecture & design practice. This role leads multi‑disciplinary architectural, master planning, landscape and interior design teams across multiple offices, ensuring design quality, client satisfaction, operational performance, and alignment with AECOM’s wider business strategy.
The Head of Architecture & Design will also play a key role in business development, major pursuits, key client relationships, talent strategy, and practice-wide innovation.

Leadership & Strategy
• Define and deliver the strategic vision for the Architecture & Design practice across the UK & Ireland.
• Lead, inspire, and develop high‑performing architecture, master planning, landscape and interior design teams across multiple studios.

• Drive market positioning and growth across priority sectors (e.g., Transportation, Defence, Healthcare, Commercial, Education, Mixed‑Use).
• Lead major pursuits, bids, and proposal strategies in partnership with the Work Winning team.
• Develop and maintain senior‑level client relationships, acting as a trusted advisor.
• Identify and pursue new market opportunities, strategic partnerships, and frameworks.
Project & Design Leadership
• Provide oversight on major architectural & design commissions, ensuring quality, risk management, compliance, and design integrity.
• Serve as Design Authority or Technical Reviewer on complex, high‑profile projects.
• Promote integrated, multi‑disciplinary working alongside engineering, digital, planning, and advisory teams.
Operational & Financial Management
• Accountable for practice‑wide financial performance, revenue forecasting, utilisation, and profitability.
• Oversee resource planning, project staffing, and capacity management.
• Implement consistent operational standards, QA/QC processes, and best practice delivery tools.
People & Talent Development
• Lead talent strategy for the Architecture & Design practice including recruitment, retention, succession planning, and early careers development.
• Foster a diverse, inclusive, supportive studio culture.
• Promote professional accreditation, CPD, and career progression pathways.
Digital, Sustainability & Innovation
• Champion digital and AI design tools (Revit, BIM, parametric design, digital twins).
• Embed sustainability principles aligned to AECOM’s ESG and net‑zero goals.
• Encourage research, thought leadership, and new ways of working.

Qualifications
• Chartered Architect (ARB / RIBA Part III), Masterplanner/Urban Designer (MRTPI) or Landscape professional (CMLI).
• Significant experience in leading architectural, masterplan or urban design teams at a senior or director level.
• Demonstrable track record in delivering major projects and managing large multi‑disciplinary teams.
• Strong commercial acumen with experience in P&L responsibility.
• Proven business development and client relationship management experience.
• Excellent communication, negotiation, and strategic leadership skills.
• Experience with BIM and digital design workflows.
Preferred Experience
• Experience working within large consultancy or multi‑disciplinary environments.
• Established reputation and network within UK architecture, masterplanning, urban design or landscape design markets.
• Experience with major complex infrastructure, defence, transportation, healthcare or large‑scale commercial/mixed‑use schemes.
• Familiarity with ISO 19650, UK building regulations, government frameworks, and procurement routes.

About This Job
Role Overview
The Senior PACS Implementation Engineer leads the build, integration, migration, and technical onboarding of customer environments onto the InSight PACS platform, acting as the technical expert for healthcare system commissioning and interoperability across NHS trusts, private healthcare providers, and third-party suppliers. The role is primarily hands-on and technical, with the successful candidate also coordinating the implementation team's day-to-day technical delivery and providing mentoring to less experienced engineers. Team leadership is a meaningful part of the role but remains secondary to its core focus on technical delivery.
Key Responsibilities
• Own end-to-end technical delivery of PACS build, integration, and migration projects, acting as the subject matter expert for DICOM, HL7, and healthcare interoperability standards across customer and partner environments.
• Design and troubleshoot integrations between PACS, RIS, EPR, VNA, and third-party clinical systems, translating customer workflows into effective, operationally sound technical solutions.
• Plan and execute imaging data migrations, including querying and troubleshooting the underlying databases, to ensure data quality and minimal disruption to clinical services.
• Lead day-to-day coordination of the implementation team's workload across build, integration, and migration activities, providing direct technical leadership, mentoring, and escalation support to engineers.
• Partner with Product, Engineering, Operations, and Client Experience teams to improve integration capabilities, maintain technical documentation, and support pre-sales and tender activities.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications and Experience
• 5+ years of experience implementing, integrating, or migrating PACS, RIS, VNA, or other healthcare imaging solutions.
• Strong working knowledge of DICOM services (C-Store, C-Find, C-Move, Modality Worklist) and practical experience with HL7 messaging in healthcare integration contexts.
• Strong SQL and database skills, including the ability to query, interrogate, and troubleshoot databases underpinning PACS and integration platforms.
• Direct experience with PACS build, configuration, and system commissioning within a regulated healthcare environment.
• Demonstrated experience leading, coordinating, or mentoring engineers within a technical delivery team.
Preferred Qualifications & Special Requirements
• Experience working with NHS organisations, including familiarity with NHS procurement processes and digital/information governance requirements.
• Knowledge of cloud-hosted healthcare applications and services.
• Experience with imaging archive consolidation or VNA migration programmes.
• Exposure to contributing to architectural standards or reference architectures (on-premises, hybrid, or cloud-based).
• Relevant project delivery, implementation, or healthcare IT certifications.
Travel Requirements  - minimal, occasional visits to Basingstoke office for training & collaboration days

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/universityofthe.description_excerpt:
About This Job
About us: The University’s Health and Safety Team have an exciting opportunity for an experienced health and safety professional who is looking to further develop their career in a future-focussed University. Through our work the University has already achieved a strong devolved health and safety approach to ensure collective leadership on this critical agenda and to support staff and student engagement. As the University looks ahead to 2030 and the implementation of its Strategy 2030, there will be a focused continual improvement on health and safety. This will be achieved through the implementation of the ‘Health, Safety and Workplace Wellbeing’ Roadmap 2030’ which has eight objectives and also annually set milestones to ensure this improvement.
The development and implementation of this ambitious Roadmap is driven by the Health and Safety Team. We are a small team of health, safety and fire professionals who provide a crucial service to the University in shaping and driving its health and safety culture and ensuring that it remains a sustained strategic priority. We strive to ensure this through robust strategies and policies, strong leadership, sound governance, excellent professional advice, targeted coaching and training and reliable performance monitoring and measurement.
As a Team we take pride in ensuring a professional and courteous approach at all times, we work in partnership with our customers and seek to ensure our communication is jargon free and risk proportionate. We aim to engage and encourage ownership and above all ensure the sharing of best practice across the University to build a perpetual health and safety culture.
About you: As a Health and Safety Adviser you will play a vital role in the Health and Safety Team and will help to ensure the delivery of the Health, Safety and Wellbeing Roadmap through direct work with our University customers and partners. You will provide a proactive and professional ‘business partner’ service to one of the University’s largest professional services, Estates and Facilities.
To be successful in the role you will need to demonstrate the following experience:
·A customer-focussed, pragmatic and proactive approach to health and safety.
·The ability to work with a high level of autonomy.
·A comprehensive understanding of the risks associated with hard and soft facilities management to include construction project management, contractor management, planned maintenance, security, cleaning and catering.
·A thorough knowledge of current Health and Safety legislation, in particular construction safety and the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations.
·A detailed understanding of Health and Safety Management Systems.
·Good organisation skills, with the ability to work to tight deadlines, both prescribed and self-imposed.
·Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the demonstrable ability to produce concise written material.
This is an exciting opportunity to engage and influence at all levels and will be suited to individuals who have a real energy to drive towards a positive health and safety culture and corresponding behaviours.
About UWE Bristol: We are one of the largest providers of Higher Education in the South West with over 30,000 students, 250,000 alumni and 3,800 staff. We are both globally connected and regionally embedded, with strong employer and partner connections. Our staff and students come from over 160 countries making this a diverse, dynamic and rewarding place to work and study.
This post is based at our lively Frenchay campus though there will be travel required to all UWE Bristol Campuses. At the Frenchay campus we have invested in the latest facilities and resources to give both our staff and students access to everything they need to succeed – with £300m having been invested recently on new state-of-the-art learning spaces and accommodation while incredible new facilities continue to be developed to enhance our offer even further.
In addition to progressive pay rates, UWE Bristol offers a wide range of employee benefits.

About This Job
Start here. Grow here.
Within our Environment & Energy (E&E) Business Lines, we are creating opportunities and delivering sustainable solutions for our clients in response to some of the world's most pressing challenges, including climate change, water scarcity and the energy transition.​
The Role:
Our Water sector is a key growth priority for Environment & Energy, presenting exciting opportunities to deliver innovative, sustainable and commercially successful solutions for our clients.
The water industry is undergoing a period of significant transformation, creating both challenges and opportunities:
• Significant change due to the Governments desire for greater public control.
• Considerable increased spending across AMP8, with the water sector competing with other sectors for resources.
• Significant opportunities for the Environmental business to support the Strategic Resource Options programme and other major programmes.
• Opportunities to extend our capability in water resources and nature-based solutions to our wider client base across Europe.
As one of our identified high growth sectors in Environment & Energy, we are seeking a Water Sector Lead to serve as the primary ambassador for Water within Environment & Energy Europe, responsible for shaping the sector’s growth strategy, building strategic client relationships, and ensuring Environment & Energy is positioned as a partner of choice in the market.
The success of this external facing role will require a combination of visible market profile and collaboration with stakeholders across the wider business. Reporting to the Environment & Energy Strategy & Growth Director for EUR&I, you will also be a member of the Environment & Energy Sales Senior Leadership Team, helping to shape our strategic direction and future growth.
Key Responsibilities:
• Provide strategic leadership for the sector, setting clear priorities and aligning activities to Environment & Energy Europe business objectives with a focus on UK and Ireland in 2027.

• Act as the figurehead for the sector, representing AECOM at industry events, conferences, and client forums to raise our profile in the sector demonstrating our technical excellence and innovation.

• Lead development and implementation of an Environment & Energy sector-specific growth plan, including client engagement strategies, targeted pursuits, strategic initiatives (including emerging areas to pivot into) and positioning for key frameworks across all Environment & Energy disciplines.
• Build and maintain strategic client relationships across the sector, fostering trust, collaboration, and repeat business.

• Support Environment & Energy priorities and campaigns relevant to the sector e.g. Advisory, Infrastructure Investment, Design & Build.
• Set the tone, celebrate success and create a positive culture across the sector in Environment & Energy business lines.

Support first line teams to identify and mitigate regulatory risks.

Draft regulatory compliance policies and guidance.

Lead obligations mapping for new product offering(s)

Understand and apply the relevant aspects of the operational resilience requirements

Interpret consumer duty and conduct requirements

Work closely with the wider regulatory team to manage our policy framework, FCA regulatory engagement, and conduct reporting.

About This Job
The Senior AI Consultant supports clients in modernising their organisations through AI by conducting in-depth analyses of complex needs and proposing strategic solutions grounded in benchmarks, evidence, and operational reality. Drawing on AI expertise and consulting experience, you enrich recommendations, challenge stakeholders to think harder about the problems worth solving, and guide teams through the change that AI adoption demands. You formalise high-quality deliverables, evaluate the medium- and long-term impact of what you recommend, and ensure clients are satisfied with both the journey and the outcome.
This role is client-facing. In most AI engagements you will be the senior SQLI voice in the room, supported by architects and engineers from across the Data & AI service line and the wider SQLI group. You will work closely with the Service Line Manager on offer development and with solution architects on solution design.
You will also help shape the practice itself. New accelerators, points of view, and reusable IP come out of the work you do with clients. We want someone who treats that as part of the job, not a side project.
What you will do
•
Conduct in-depth analysis of client needs and context, identify where AI delivers real value, and challenge stakeholders to develop solutions that address the actual problem rather than the surface symptom
•
Design, formalise, and propose AI solutions based on benchmarks, evidence, and feedback, with a credible path from business objective to measurable outcome
•
Advise clients on strategic and operational decision-making, assessing the medium- and long-term impact of AI adoption on their organisation, operating model, and commercials
•
Lead AI workshops, presentations, and pitches with senior client stakeholders, including non-technical audiences
•
Support change management around AI adoption, lead working groups, ensure skills transfer to client teams, and promote buy-in across the organisations we work with
•
Shape commercial proposals together with the Service Line Manager, contributing the technical and solution narrative across the full sales-to-delivery cycle
•
Work with solution architects and engineering teams to validate technical feasibility and shape solution architectures at a level you can defend in client conversations
•
Help shape new AI offers, accelerators, and reusable assets for the practice, and contribute to the internal promotion of SQLI’s AI capability
•
Ensure quality of deliverables, meet deadlines, and maintain a close advisory relationship with clients beyond individual engagements

Qualifications
Must have
•
Demonstrated experience advising enterprise clients on AI, with a portfolio of engagements you can speak to in depth
•
Strong client focus, with the ability to understand business objectives, KPIs, and operational context, and plan strategies that connect AI capabilities to measurable outcomes
•
Solid understanding of the full sales-to-delivery cycle in a consulting or agency setting
•
Excellent communication skills, able to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and adapt the message to the room
•
AI-first working style. You use AI tools (Claude in particular, also ChatGPT and others) daily to brainstorm, research, generate, and accelerate your own work, while staying in control and challenging the output when it is wrong
•
Practical understanding of Claude Code, Cowork, plugins and skills, MCP connectors, and what an AI agent actually is and is not
•
Technical background sufficient to discuss enterprise architecture, integrations, and data flows at a senior level, even if you are not the deepest technical voice in the room
•
Working understanding of how AI delivers value in the enterprise and where it fails, across delivery acceleration, customer-facing applications, and agentic workflows
•
Native-level English fluency, both spoken and written
•
Eligible to work in the United Kingdom
Nice to have
•
Background from an e-commerce agency, or from an AI, agentic, or workflow automation consultancy
•
Track record of identifying and optimising business operations and workflows using AI
•
Strong presentation craft, including the ability to create engaging slides, diagrams, and visual narratives
•
Experience contributing to or co-authoring commercial proposals, particularly outside the standard day-rate model (packaged, subscription, outcome-based)
•
Experience shaping practice IP: accelerators, points of view, methodologies, reusable assets
•
Working French

Additional Information
How we will work together
You will report into the Data & AI service line leadership. You will work alongside architects and engineers across the Data & AI service line and the wider SQLI group, and contribute to the International AI community. There is real scope to shape the role over the next twelve months, including progression to Principal level as the practice scales.
How to apply
Send a short note covering:
•
One or two AI engagements you have shaped, what the business problem was, and how you measured success
•
A view on where you think enterprise AI delivers real value today and where the hype exceeds the reality
•
Your notice period and earliest start date
Why you’ll love working at SQLI?
• A flexible remote working policy: 3 days per week
• Continuous learning opportunities and certifications to support your development
• Personalised support: career follow-up, diverse projects, and strong team collaboration
• Regular rituals: internal communications on tech and AI topics, internal events, and meet-ups

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/bankerswithoutb.description_excerpt:
About This Job
Empowering Financial Professionals to Lead Sustainable Transformation
The BwB Fellows Programme offers an exceptional opportunity for experienced financial professionals to contribute to innovative, high-impact projects, receive mentorship from respected industry leaders, and join a driven global community that is dedicated to advancing environmental and social good.
Programme Aim
This exclusive two-year programme is designed to nurture future leaders in sustainable finance by empowering them to employ their existing skills in new ways and gain new knowledge and experience through strategic-level engagement with BwB’s innovative initiatives. The programme’s focus is on strategic input, high-level advisory work, and thought leadership, rather than operational execution.
What to Expect from the BwB Fellows Programme
•
Meaningful Engagement with Sustainability Projects: Fellows contribute up to 10 hours per month to support transformative projects that employ innovative strategies, instruments, and structures to mobilise capital for social and environmental impact across a diverse range of sectors and geographies. Projects may involve:
• Structuring innovative financial mechanisms for climate resilience and biodiversity.
• Developing investment frameworks for nature-based solutions and sustainable infrastructure.
• Collaborating with public and private stakeholders on blended finance initiatives.
• Supporting public finance strategies to unlock capital for underserved communities.
• Engaging in development finance projects mobilising resources across emerging markets.
• Mutual Mentorship and Knowledge Exchange: Fellows will receive direct mentorship from BwB’s leadership, senior ambassadors, and members of the Global Expert Group, who are recognised experts in finance, policy, and sustainability. At the same time, Fellows will be asked to provide mentorship to BwB analytical team members, drawing on their practical, market-driven experience to share expertise in areas such as: capital markets and financial structuring; sovereign and sub-sovereign debt; blended finance and impact investing; asset and risk management; and development finance institution project development and execution.
• Access to Exclusive Networking Opportunities and Events: Fellows will have opportunities to interact with members of BwB’s Global Expert Group through events such as small group sessions and roundtable discussions. Fellows will also be invited to BwB’s annual retreat – an immersive gathering designed to foster collaboration, develop new ideas, celebrate progress, and exchange experiences and insights.
• Lifelong Membership in BwB Alumni Group: Upon completing the two-year programme, Fellows transition into the BwB Alumni Group, enabling them to maintain valuable connections and draw on the collective expertise of individuals at the forefront of sustainable finance.

Qualifications
Eligibility
• Applicants must:
• Be currently working in investment banking (sell-side), asset management (buy-side), public finance, or a development finance institution.
• Have a minimum of eight years of relevant experience.
• Have a demonstrable passion for sustainability and financial innovation and a strong rationale for becoming a BwB Fellow.
• Time commitment: Up to 10 hours per month over the two-year programme, with flexibility to accommodate full-time employment.
• Compliance requirements: Formally commit to upholding BwB’s compliance standards, including adherence to NDAs, conflict of interest policies, and fit and proper requirements.
• Employer engagement: Fellows are encouraged to discuss participation with their employers to ensure alignment with internal policies.
• Financial contribution: A one-time fee of £10,000 (or equivalent in USD/EUR) is required upon acceptance to the programme.
Accessibility and Scholarship Options
At BwB, we believe that sustainable finance should be driven by a diverse and inclusive network of professionals. To ensure accessibility for individuals who may not be in a position to meet the financial commitment, a limited number of scholarship and fee-adjusted places are available. Candidates are encouraged to apply for assistance if they:
• Can demonstrate exceptional potential to contribute to driving sustainable finance.
• Have a compelling rationale for participating but face financial constraints.
Candidates should indicate their interest in a scholarship or fee adjustment during the application process by providing a brief statement outlining their situation. Scholarships will be awarded based on merit, potential impact, and commitment to BwB’s mission.

Additional Information
Participation Scope
As established above, the programme’s focus is on strategic input, high-level advisory work, and thought leadership, rather than operational execution. Fellows will provide insights and contribute to shaping BwB’s initiatives to help deliver high-impact outcomes, maintaining a hands-off position as regards direct implementation of project work.
Applications, Selection, and Intake
The BwB Fellows Programme is an unparallelled opportunity for driven individuals to help shape the future of sustainable finance and make a meaningful contribution to positive change.
Applications are accepted on a rolling basis, with Fellows joining in spring and autumn each year. The programme is highly selective, offering limited placements annually to ensure Fellows enjoy meaningful, individualised experiences.
Eligible individuals who wish to be considered for this unique programme should submit the following information to begin the candidate review process:
• A detailed statement of interest outlining their passion for sustainability.
• A record of relevant experience and achievements.

About This Job
Your mission
As Senior Research Lead for Grow, you’ll own research’s strategic contribution across the entire business area. You’ll identify and initiate the research programmes that matter most, connecting questions and opportunities across multiple teams.
Your focus will be on where Grow needs to go, what it needs to learn to move forward and driving change. You’ll ensure research anticipates hurdles, identifies future opportunities and helps the organisation make confident decisions.
You’ll work with the cross-functional teams that make up Grow. Together, they’re rethinking how people can earn a return on all their money, regardless of currency, goal or risk appetite. You’ll initially lead one or two researchers, supporting their performance, development and progression while setting clear direction for the team’s work. Alongside this leadership, you’ll continue to plan and deliver strategically important research yourself.
Success at this level means research is integral to how Grow sets direction and prioritises opportunities.
Here’s how you’ll make an impact
•
Defining research direction: Set clear direction across teams, connecting customer evidence to Grow’s product and business goals
•
Raising research quality and maturity: Set and uphold high standards, champion user-centred decision-making and improve research capability across teams
•
Strengthening research practice: Bring together people, processes, tools and standards so research is focused, efficient and consistently high quality
•
Leading through people: Develop researchers and future research leaders, cultivate a strong leadership culture and take responsibility for performance and impact
•
Using evidence to influence: Use evidence to shape core product features, multi-team roadmaps and senior stakeholder decisions
•
Building compelling narratives: Create a clear picture of the future that aligns teams and inspires Wise’s senior leaders to act
•
Managing interdependencies: Align research priorities across teams, resolve dependencies and create clarity around shared decisions
•
Using modern tools thoughtfully: Set direction for the responsible use of AI and emerging tools where they improve speed, quality or impact without weakening research rigour or judgement
About you
•
You have 10+ years’ research experience, including leading researchers across multiple teams or complex product areas
•
You have a track record of raising research quality and maturity across teams by improving craft, processes, tools and standards
•
You can shape research and product strategy across a business area and influence senior stakeholders through compelling evidence and storytelling
•
You can connect customer evidence to business outcomes and identify opportunities for research to create new value
•
You can lead diverse teams through change, complexity and ambiguity while maintaining clear direction and high standards
•
You can develop strong researchers and future leaders through clear expectations, thoughtful coaching and accountable performance management
•
You can navigate competing priorities and resolve complex people and stakeholder challenges while maintaining trust and cohesion
And as a heads up, this role probably isn't for you if:
•
Your experience is primarily in market research or academia, without demonstrable experience leading user research in technology or product teams
•
You want a management-only role and no longer want to plan or deliver research yourself

The Clinical Standards Lead role will work closely with new and experienced Functional Assessors to provide supervision and feedback, utilising quality and productivity data to enable professional development in line with the Performance Excellence Framework.

IFS builds enterprise software for asset-intensive and service industries: ERP, Enterprise Asset Management, and Field Service Management. inference workloads

Data foundations: pipelines and lakehouse patterns (Microsoft Fabric/OneLake, Databricks, or equivalents), streaming and event-driven integration where the problem demands it

What sets candidates apart
•
Classical ML depth alongside GenAI: forecasting, anomaly detection, predicThe role
•
This is a hands-on architect role that grows into a player-coach role. You will start as the senior technical individual contributor in the CTO Office and then hire and lead a small team of engineers built in your image.
•
The unit takes on whatever matters most at the time. One month that is a production-grade agentic system with a frontier model provider, the next it is an architecture review of a platform under consideration, an internal AI tool the whole company adopts, or a technical escalation from a strategic customer. There is no standing backlog to hide behind. You go in, learn the domain fast, deliver something real in weeks, and hand it over or harden it.
•
We are explicit about the calibre we are hiring for. The team exists to produce output that would normally take a squad a quarter, in a fraction of the time, at production quality. If that sounds exhausting rather than energising, this is the wrong role.
What you will do
•
Own architecture and delivery on the CTO Office's highest-priority technical projects, end to end
•
Write and review code daily; the role never becomes slideware
•
Design and ship agentic and LLM-based systems to production standard: retrieval at scale, evals, guardrails, security and identity, monitoring and auditability
•
Drop into unfamiliar codebases, stacks, and business domains and become dangerous within days
•
Hire, coach, and set the technical bar for a small team of applied AI engineers
•
Brief executives and senior customer stakeholders on what you built and what it means commercially

Qualifications
What we are looking for
•
15+ years building software, with architecture ownership of systems running in production at enterprise scale
•
Still keyboard-credible: you review PRs, debug agents, and ship. We will verify this in the interview process
•
Deep, current applied AI capability: production agentic systems, RAG and Graph RAG, MCP, agent runtimes, and fluency across model providers rather than loyalty to one
•
Eval fluency. You can articulate and build an evaluation strategy for an LLM system. Candidates who cannot are not a fit, regardless of seniority
•
Evidence of operating AI systems at enterprise scale, not a portfolio of PoCs
•
Range and speed: a track record of delivering across different domains, stacks, and problem shapes under time pressure
•
Experience hiring engineers and raising a team's technical standard
•
Clear written and spoken communication at executive level
Technical depth expected
•
We hire for depth per area, not a keyword count. The named tools are examples; strong equivalents are fine. Expect to be tested on the areas below, not asked whether you have heard of them.
•
Languages: expert-level Python and TypeScript for AI and product work, and the ability to read and contribute to the large enterprise codebases you will drop into (C#/.NET, Java)
•
Model providers: hands-on production work with at least 2 of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and open-weight models (direct APIs or via Azure AI Foundry, Bedrock, Vertex); tool use and function calling, structured outputs, context and token management, prompt architecture
•
Agentic systems: designing, hosting, and operating autonomous and semi-autonomous agents in production; MCP servers and clients; orchestration frameworks such as LangGraph, Pydantic AI, or provider-native SDKs; sandboxing, permissioning, and human-in-the-loop design
•
Retrieval and knowledge: RAG and Graph RAG at enterprise scale; vector and hybrid search (pgvector, OpenSearch/Elasticsearch, or dedicated stores) including chunking strategy, reranking, and distributed retrieval; knowledge graphs and entity resolution; Text-to-SQL over complex enterprise schemas
•
Evals and quality: golden datasets, regression suites, LLM-as-judge patterns, online monitoring of model behaviour; tooling such as RAGAS, promptfoo, Langfuse or LangSmith, or eval harnesses you built yourself
•
Security, identity, and governance: OAuth2/OIDC, Entra ID and service principals, secrets management; guardrails and content safety; auditability and traceability of agent decisions
•

• Experience using HSE reporting systems, performance data and digital tools to support risk based decision-making and continuous improvement

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/ifs1/7440001435.description_excerpt:
About This Job
Build and curate the ontology, knowledge graph and grounding infrastructure that let AI agents understand IFS software and reason accurately over customer data, turning what the platform already knows about itself, plus deep industry expertise, into a semantic layer other engineers and agents can trust.
Key responsibilities
•
Design and build MCP servers (Model Context Protocol, the emerging standard for exposing application capability to agents) over the product’s business objects, treating capability modelling, discoverability, versioning and backward compatibility as first-class design problems.
•
Build the write path that lets an agent safely change a customer’s operational data.
•
Design and build the semantic layer: an ontology and knowledge graph over the product, generated from what the platform already knows about itself and then curated industry by industry, in partnership with domain experts who turn tacit product knowledge into an explicit, machine-usable model.
•
Build the retrieval and grounding infrastructure that connects agents to this knowledge: embeddings, vector databases, hybrid search, chunking and indexing strategies, memory architectures, and grounding techniques that keep agent outputs accurate and traceable to source.
•
Establish data quality, provenance and versioning practices for the knowledge graph, so changes are traceable and agent behaviour built on top of it doesn't silently drift.
•
Build the skills layer that maps what someone asks for onto the correct operation and the correct sequence, with a router that picks between them.
•
Build the control plane: authentication, entitlements, agent identity, telemetry, metering, resistance to injection, and a default that denies rather than permits.
•
Build the evaluation harness that certifies agent behaviour against the real product, and improve the system against what it measures.
•
Build rapid prototypes and proofs of concept to validate emerging technology, product opportunities and customer scenarios.
•
Establish the engineering practices these systems need: evaluation, testing, observability, monitoring, governance, security and operational excellence.
•
Contribute to technical design, review other engineers’ work, and support colleagues coming into the domain.
•
Represent the work outside the team through customer engagements, demonstrations, industry events and partner collaboration.

Qualifications
Strong software engineering first. Everything else is applied on top of that.
•
Production experience building and operating enterprise systems, with real depth in distributed systems, cloud-native architectures, API and schema design, event-driven systems, security, observability and CI/CD.
•
Strong programming in a modern backend language.
•
Experience delivering AI systems built on large language models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic workflows and orchestration frameworks, including tool use, function calling, workflow orchestration and autonomous or multi-agent architectures, with the judgement to know where they fail.
•
Deep, hands-on expertise in knowledge graphs and semantic modelling: ontology design (RDF/OWL/SKOS or property-graph equivalents), taxonomy and controlled-vocabulary design, entity resolution, schema evolution and versioning, embeddings, vector databases and grounding strategies.
•
Evaluation as a discipline: experimentation, benchmarking, prompt engineering, tracing, quality measurement and agent tuning, improving an agent against evidence rather than impression.
•
Ability to design solutions that integrate enterprise applications, business processes, workflows and data platforms.
•
Comfort working directly with domain experts to translate tacit business knowledge into explicit, machine-usable models.
•
Depth in at least one of the following:
•
Tool-surface and agent-runtime engineering. MCP servers, tool ecosystems, capability modelling, discoverability, governance, versioning, backward compatibility, multi-tenancy isolation.
•
Enterprise platform depth. Oracle PL/SQL, OData, and comfort working inside large metadata-driven systems where behaviour is configured rather than coded.
Desirable
•
Experience with agent frameworks such as Semantic Kernel, Microsoft Agent Framework, LangGraph, AutoGen, PydanticAI, the OpenAI Agents SDK or CrewAI.
•
Experience building reusable AI platforms, MCP ecosystems or shared engineering capabilities used across multiple products and teams.
•
Containerised platforms and infrastructure automation: Docker, Kubernetes.
•
Experience with Azure, AWS, GCP or another hyperscale cloud platform.
•
Reverse-engineering or interpreter work.
•
Token-efficient agent design.
•
Enterprise software domains: enterprise asset management, service management, manufacturing, supply chain, aerospace and defence, energy, telecommunications, construction, industrial AI.
•
Contributions to open-source projects, technical communities, conferences, publications or standards.

Additional Information
We believe that coming together as a community, in person, is important for innovation, connection and fostering a sense of belonging. Our roles have the right balance of remote and in-office working to enable flexibility for managing your life along with ensuring a real connection with your colleagues and the broader IFS community.

About This Job
About the opportunity
Reporting into our Finance Manager, this role is responsible for the many aspects of the month end close process and for the fulfilment of other obligations such as tax and statutory reporting. We are looking for someone who is genuinely interested in the FinTech landscape, with solid financial accounting and reporting experience and a desire to support with automating and streamlining processes.
Some of the other responsibilities include :
• Managing the general ledger including overseeing the monthly balance sheet, banking and inter-company reconciliations
• Production of IFRS consolidated results and stand alone financial statements.
• Key team member involved in pro-actively ensuring the Group’s financial accounting and reporting remains compliant with the relevant accounting standards.
• Preparation of monthly financial reports covering balance sheet, profit and loss, internal management reports and cashflow statements. Completion of the monthly prepayments, accruals, journals, fixed assets and depreciation schedules.
• Liaison with external Auditors, Bank Managers, ONS and Tax specialists.
• Assisting in process improvement and systems enhancement initiatives.
• Proactively identify new initiatives that could benefit the organisation.
This role is fully remote across the UK, with occasional meet-ups at our Newcastle office.

Qualifications
What would make me a good candidate?
We are looking for curious and empathetic people. We also love to hear from people who are motivated by meaningful work, resonate with our core values, have a positive outlook, are comfortable with ambiguity and thrive working in an ever-evolving and complex environment. We are inspired by meeting big-picture thinkers and doers, people who can be both tactical and strategic, aim high and put people first in everything they do.
• A minimum of 3–5 years’ experience in an accounting role
• Experience within a Chartered Accounting firm is advantageous
• Exposure to working with the APAC region is highly desirable
• Strong commercial acumen with a solid understanding of business operations
• Highly organised and deadline-driven, with excellent attention to detail
• A critical thinker with strong problem-solving capabilities
• Confident negotiator, able to build and maintain strong working relationships
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills
• Proven ability to analyse data and identify trends, insights, and anomalies
• Advanced proficiency in Excel and financial reporting tools
• A professional accounting qualification, or actively working towards one (e.g. AAT or ACCA)
At Xplor, we believe that the best innovation and ideas happen at the intersections of our differences - people of diverse cultures, generations, disciplines, and lived experiences. So even if you think you do not tick all the boxes, we still encourage you to apply.

Additional Information
Values and Life at Xplor
Our five core values guide us from how we hire and recognise our team members to how we interact with our customers day to day:
• Find a better way
• Do the right thing
• Say it straight
• Win together
• Own the outcome
If these values sound like you, and describe people you want to work with, you will thrive at Xplor.
As an Xplorer, you will be part of a global network of talented colleagues who will support your success. We look for commonalities and shared passions and give people the tools they need to deliver great work and grow at speed.
Some of our perks and benefits are:
• Paid Parental Leave benefit programs
• #GiveBackDays/Commitment to social impact – 3 extra days off to volunteer and give back to your local community
• Ongoing dedication to Diversity & Inclusion initiatives such as D&I Council, Global Mentorship Program
• Access to free mental health support
• Flexible working arrangements
Ready to apply?
To start your application, please submit your resume, and we will be in touch as soon as we can. Please include the word "moonshot" at the top of your message to the Hiring Manager so that we know you took the time to read our job ad.
We understand that diverse candidates have diverse needs. We welcome you to inform us of any additional needs related to completing your job application or participating in the interview process, via talentsupport@xplortechnologies.com.
Before you apply
To be considered for employment, you must be legally authorised to work in the United Kingdom. This applies to remote roles too, as we can only employ people who reside within the UK. Xplor does not sponsor visas, either at the time of hire or at any later time. We're also not able to offer contractor arrangements or Employer of Record engagements for this position at this stage.
Please apply through our careers portal or external job boards only. We're unable to upload emailed applications, as our process requires you to answer screening questions directly.
We also invite you to check out our Candidate FAQs for more information about our recruitment process xplor.com/recruitment-faqs/.
Interview Recording and Background Checks
As part of our hiring process, successful candidates will be asked to complete background and identity verification checks. Many of our roles are remote, and to protect both candidates and our business from recruitment fraud, we may record video interviews via Microsoft Teams during the process. We keep any recordings and related data only for as long as the hiring process is active and do not retain them afterwards.
EEO and Artificial Intelligence
We believe in transparent hiring. We use an applicant tracking system with artificial intelligence-enabled features to support our recruitment process, but our recruitment team makes all hiring decisions after human review. We do not rely on artificial intelligence to make final hiring decisions. Find our Candidate AI Usage guidelines here.
Xplor is dedicated to attracting, retaining and developing our people regardless of gender identity, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability and age. We encourage applications from all sectors of the community.
We make it a priority to respond to every applicant.

About This Job
As a Summer Intern at TTP, your work over 10 weeks will see you working alongside consultants from a range of academic backgrounds, from engineers and computer scientists to physicists and biologists – experiencing technology consulting first hand. Over the course of your placement, you will contribute directly to live client and internal projects, applying your own knowledge to solve problems, build prototypes in the lab, and explore new areas of technology.
You’ll combine using your engineering skillset to support multi-disciplinary project teams inventing new products and technologies, with learning more about the commercial acumen that drives projects forward. You’ll demonstrate leadership, build collaborative relationships with stakeholders and ultimately work towards understanding the industries and disciplines we work across.
We believe growth happens best in a collaborative environment where knowledge is shared freely and curiosity is encouraged – our non-hierarchical culture gives you the freedom to explore projects that reflect your own interest. You'll receive mentorship and guidance when needed, but also the space and encouragement to take ownership of your work.
By the end of the internship, you will have first-hand experience of how engineering and science are applied in a commercial context, as well as a clear sense of what it’s like to work in a fast-paced, innovative environment like ours. Our internships are also a great pathway into a career, as we consider all our interns for graduate roles.

Qualifications
•
Deep intellectual curiosity and inventiveness, with a desire to understand how things work at a fundamental level. You should have an academic record that reflects your capacity for rigorous, first-principles thinking - being on track for a minimum 2:1 in AI/ML, Engineering or Physics, or a closely related discipline, with strong accompanying A-Levels (or equivalent, i.e. IB qualifications).
•
Commercially aware and entrepreneurial, excited by the opportunity to turn breakthrough technologies into real-world products, ventures, and impact.
•
Proactive and self-starting, with a strong sense of personal responsibility and a drive to make things happen.
•
Collaborative and emotionally intelligent, able to build trust, influence stakeholders, energise those around you, and communicate complex technical ideas with clarity, empathy, and precision, regardless of your audience's background.
•
Strategic and systems-minded, able to see the bigger picture, anticipate challenges and opportunities while considering the commercial aspects of technology product development, and navigate ambiguity while keeping priorities sharp and focused.
We're looking for candidates who want to impact the industry both commercially and technically; those who don't just solve problems - but who seek them out, thrive on them, and elevate those around them while doing so.
We recruit on a rolling basis, so although there is no application deadline, the advert will close once all spaces have been filled. We recommend applying early for the best chance. You must have completed at least 2 years of your degree when your internship begins, so students at the beginning of second year are welcome to apply.
The length of this internship can be flexible, but we ask for minimum commitment of 8 weeks and recommend 10, starting in July 2027.

Additional Information
TTP operates from an award-winning campus in green surroundings, just south of Cambridge. This is a paid internship with generous benefits, including free accommodation in Cambridge (subject to availability) and free lunch, as well as a wide range of clubs to join covering sports and social activities.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/cliffordchance/.description_excerpt:
About This Job
The role
The Legal Technology Advisor (LTA) is an ambitious, analytical delivery specialist, passionate about digital transformation—including the practical use of Artificial Intelligence—who operates at the intersection of law and technology across One Europe. Embedded within designated Global Business Units (GBUs) throughout the region, the LTA collaborates with deal teams and litigation teams to implement technology solutions in real time, configuring tools during active matters to ensure seamless delivery. Acting as the bridge between client needs and Clifford Chance’s technology capabilities, the LTA scopes, advises on, and deploys technology-enabled solutions that improve efficiency, reduce risk, and contribute to revenue growth across European jurisdictions. This role drives adoption of the firm’s legal technology toolkit, delivers at the pace of client needs, and channels market and front-line insights from across One Europe to Product Management and Legal Technology Advisory leadership, helping to shape the firm’s innovation pipeline.
Key responsibilities
Delivery and Collaboration
• Act as the first point of contact for matter teams within the assigned GBU seeking technology‑enabled solutions; assess requirements, define scope and recommend appropriate tools and approaches.
• Design and deliver technology‑assisted workflows for live matters (e.g., document/contract review and analysis, due diligence, document automation, transaction management, litigation/eDiscovery, collaboration and workflow tools), ensuring high‑quality, compliant execution.
• Configure, integrate and optimise existing solutions to meet matter requirements; document functional requirements and enhancement requests; work with Product Management, IT and vendors on pilots and deployments.
• Identify and support power users of key legal technology solutions to help scale delivery capabilities across the GBU.
• Maintain clear documentation for solution configurations, matter playbooks and client engagement materials; share lessons learnt through the Legal Technology Advisory Community of Practice.
Client and Business Engagement
• Build strong relationships with partners and associates, serve as a trusted advisor and deliver at the pace of the client’s needs.
• Prepare and deliver tailored client‑facing demonstrations, proofs of concept and proposals that evidence value, differentiation and time‑to‑value.
• Support pricing and scoping of technology components in pitches, proposals and panel submissions, working with partners and commercial teams.
• Coordinate with relevant business stakeholders to embed legal technology into delivery and client strategies.
Strategic Insight and Market Awareness
• Monitor legal market trends, competitive activity and emerging technologies; identify process improvement opportunities and report local emerging technology solutions so they can be considered in the firm’s innovation pipeline.
• Capture and share success stories, usage insights and client feedback to inform go‑to‑market materials and the product roadmap.
• Balance immediate client demands with opportunities for broader business transformation, articulating practical, scalable solutions and change impacts.
Legal Technology Advisory
• Develop a deep understanding of lawyers' and clients' needs within the assigned GBU, promoting the benefits of the firm's legal technology toolkit and advising on optimal usage scenarios.
• Design, develop and apply technology solutions on-the-fly to support and deliver live matter work.
• Drive metrics‑driven adoption of existing solutions, prioritising engagement by demand, impact and readiness; address challenges collaboratively with Product Management teams.
• Assist with the introduction, deployment and communication of new solutions, focusing on end‑to‑end legal service delivery processes.
• Deliver tailored presentations and demos of the firm’s legal technology toolkit, including advanced specialist solutions and AI tools.
• Ensure solutions and workflows comply with firm policies, client requirements, data privacy and information security standards; identify delivery risks early and propose mitigations.
Committee and Group Participation
• Actively participate in the Legal Technology Advisory Community of Practice.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
• Revenue generation directly attributable to the application of legal technology.
• Reduction in matter write-offs through improved efficiency and effective deployment of legal technology solutions.
• Success in winning client matters and panel appointments specifically due to demonstrated legal technology capabilities.
• Positive client feedback and satisfaction regarding technology-driven solutions and engagements.

Qualifications
Your experience
Skills:
• Demonstrable experience advising on and delivering legal technology within a professional services context (preferably legal or consulting).
• Hands‑on expertise across tools such as contract analysis and review platforms, document automation, transaction management, litigation/eDiscovery, workflow and collaboration solutions; strong familiarity with Microsoft 365 and the Power Platform is advantageous.
• Knowledge of AI and data‑driven solutions (including Generative AI, NLP and machine learning) and their practical application to legal workflows.
• Strength in requirements gathering, solution scoping, process mapping and change management; able to translate complex needs into practical, scalable solutions.
• Experience with Agile delivery practices and collaboration tools (e.g., Agile Central, JIRA); comfortable working with Product Management, IT and vendors.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills; able to explain technical concepts in plain language and tailor style to partners, lawyers, clients and business stakeholders.
• High‑quality written communication skills, including preparation of internal communications, and client‑facing materials.
• Strong analytical skills with the ability to manipulate data quickly and accurately; confident using metrics to drive prioritisation and decisions.
• Commercial awareness and insight into how legal technology impacts client outcomes and law firm economics.
• Proactive problem‑solver with entrepreneurial drive; able to manage multiple engagements, prioritise effectively and see initiatives through to completion.
• Credibility and intellectual rigour, with strong listening skills and a commitment to continuous learning and innovation.
• Confident, positive approach; comfortable interacting with individuals at all levels of the organisation.
Qualifications:
• Educated to degree level or equivalent experience.
• Fluent in English; additional European languages are an advantage.
• Client‑facing interaction or consulting experience is a plus.

Additional Information
Hybrid working
This role follows our balanced hybrid working approach and as long as business needs allow, you will be supported to work
