About This Job
Role Overview
We are looking for an Assistant Manager to join our growing Restructuring Advisory team. You will work on a wide range of assignments across both advisory and formal engagements. These will include pre-lend and short-term cash flow forecast reviews, alongside options reviews for distressed or stressed companies.
You will also support the management of a portfolio of insolvency cases, including administrations, liquidations, receiverships and CVAs, working with senior members of the team to ensure statutory compliance and effective stakeholder engagement throughout.
Key Responsibilities
• Analyse, present and provide commentary on financial information including management accounts, audited accounts, budgets and forecasts
• Identify and comment on unusual trends or variances and their potential causes by understanding the operations of the business and linking this to the financial information
• Review forecast financial models including the structure of the model and how assumptions are modelled
• Support the management and progression of a portfolio of insolvency cases including administrations, CVLs, WUCs, CVAs and BKYs
• Assist with case progression and ensure compliance with insolvency legislation
• Contribute to case planning, strategy and execution, taking responsibility for assigned areas of work
• Draft and review high-quality reports and presentations for internal and external stakeholders
• Liaise with stakeholders including directors, creditors, legal advisors, accountants and agents
• Liaise with other FRP teams where cross-pillar expertise and experience are required
• Undertake and review analysis and investigations into financial affairs and transactions, obtaining legal advice where required
• Identify and escalate potential risks and/or legal issues where appropriate
• Support and supervise junior team members and contribute to their development
• Contribute to internal training, process improvement and technical updates

Qualifications
• Chartered Accountant (ACA/ACCA qualified)
• Relevant professional qualifications (e.g. CPI, JIEB) advantageous
• Relevant experience working on insolvency cases or restructuring assignments
• Strong technical knowledge of UK insolvency legislation and procedures
• Excellent written and report-writing skills
• Proficiency in Excel with strong core maths skills
• Collaborative team player with a proactive and adaptable approach, capable of managing competing priorities and delivering under pressure

Additional Information
Our Values
• Straightforward: We provide clear, no-nonsense advice
• Confident: Our guidance is backed by expertise and evidence
• Pragmatic: We focus on practical solutions and tangible outcomes
• Real: We are professional yet approachable, understanding the challenges our clients face
Our Commitment to You and the Environment

You'll own the end-to-end accounting for a group of more complex business areas. Entity and process ownership

Balance sheet integrity and review

Statutory reporting, audit and controls

Continuous improvement and change

Engineering UK. This is a business-critical leadership role responsible for driving the growth, performance, and strategic direction of our MEP practice across the UK, with teams based in London, Manchester, Glasgow, and Edinburgh.

What we are looking for
Hopefully you’re interested and excited about what your days at Atelier Ten will look like. We do have a few items on our wish list for you to become the next great “ATenner”.

In addition to contract work, you will provide advice on legal and regulatory developments affecting the firm, develop practical guidance and policies, and help promote a strong culture of compliance, risk awareness and operational excellence.

Desirable

Who we are?
Linklaters is a global law firm, providing legal services in 20 countries and through 30 offices.
We have been named as one of The Times’ Top 50 Employers for Gender Equality for the 10th year running, recognised by Stonewall as a top 10 employer for LGBTQ+ inclusion, and by the Social Mobility Employer Index as a top employer for advancing social mobility.
Role overview
We are seeking an experienced Paralegal/Support Lawyer to join our Structured Finance Group. The successful candidate will support a broad range of structured finance and leveraged finance transactions, working closely with lawyers, clients, financial institutions and external advisers to deliver transactions efficiently and within tight deadlines.
This role would suit someone with prior transactional banking experience, ideally gained within a leading international law firm, who enjoys working in a fast-paced, deal-driven environment. Many transactions are time-sensitive and involve managing multiple competing priorities, making this an excellent opportunity for an individual who thrives under pressure and enjoys seeing matters through from inception to closing.
Given the international nature of the practice, flexibility to work outside standard UK business hours on occasion is important, including regular collaboration with colleagues and clients across Asia-Pacific time zones.
Key responsibilities
• Support the execution of structured finance and leveraged finance transactions from signing through to closing.
• Assist with the preparation, review and management of transaction documentation, ensuring accuracy and timely delivery of key work products.
• Coordinate transaction processes and manage critical workstreams across multiple stakeholders.
• Prepare and maintain transaction checklists, conditions precedent trackers, closing agendas and execution documents.
• Manage signing and closing processes, ensuring all documentation is executed correctly and transaction milestones are met.
• Liaise with clients, lenders, borrowers, trustees, financial institutions and external advisers to facilitate the smooth progression of transactions.
• Monitor transaction timetables and proactively identify and escalate issues that may impact delivery deadlines.
• Manage post-completion requirements, filing obligations and maintenance of transaction records.
• Provide regular transaction status updates to lawyers and other stakeholders.
Candidate requirements
• LPC, SQE, law degree or equivalent legal qualification (including foreign-qualified lawyers).
• Experience supporting complex financing transactions, including structured finance, leveraged finance, banking or other debt-related transactions.
• Strong understanding of transaction lifecycles, legal documentation and deal execution processes.
• Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple live transactions simultaneously.
• Comfortable working to tight deadlines within a high-volume, fast-paced transactional environment.
• A proactive and resilient approach, with the ability to remain calm and effective under pressure.
• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with experience liaising with lawyers, clients, financial institutions and external advisers.
• Flexibility to work longer hours when required to meet transaction deadlines and support cross-border deal teams, including overlap with Asia-Pacific time zones.
• Highly detail-oriented, with a strong commitment to quality and client service.
Third-party provider
Linklaters engages with a third-party provider for the provision of contractor and temporary staff. Therefore, upon acceptance of a temporary role at Linklaters, you will be engaged under a contract for services through our preferred third-party provider. You will not be employed by Linklaters, or have any employment or worker relationship with Linklaters.
Technical Skills
This list of duties and responsibilities above is not exhaustive.  It is intended to describe the general content of, and requirements for, the performance of this job. As such, the role may also include the undertaking of additional tasks as required.
Application Policy
Applications and CVs (direct or via agency) are only accepted online via the portal. Queries related to this role must be directed to the recruitment team ( tempbtrecruitment@linklaters.com) and not partners, practices or stakeholders.

Do you want to use physics and mathematics to solve real world problems? Are you looking for a career in industry where you can continue to develop your scientific skills and knowledge?
Viridien operates in a rapidly changing global technology market providing high-end scientific solutions primarily to the natural resources and energy sectors. A focus on innovation, quality, and client service are key to our success—supported by a culture of learning, collaboration, and ambition.
You will use the latest signal processing, modelling and imaging technology and some of the most advanced high-performance computing facilities in the world to build high-resolution 3D seismic images & models of subsurface geology and rock properties for our clients.

• Signal processing, modelling and imaging
• Technical innovation, creative problem solving and critical thinking
• Building and maintaining long-term client relationships through service excellence
• Management of complex technical projects
• Effective communication and collaboration with team members and clients
• Cultural awareness through training & interaction with global clients and teams
Later in your career, you will have opportunities to develop leadership and management skills, publish papers and present at industry conferences
Most people who start with Viridien come from outside the earth sciences; we will provide all necessary training in geology and geophysics.

This role is aimed at recent graduates and final-year students with a Bachelors, integrated or postgraduate Masters or PhD in Physics, Geophysics, or Mathematics, or in Earth Sciences, Natural Sciences or Engineering with significant physics content.

• Your interest in learning and curiosity about how things work
• Your ability to communicate technical concepts

• Start date: September 6th 2027 although we can be flexible around start date if a later start date is desired or necessary.

• Explore our Careers page, Gradcracker Hub, and Viridien Stories to learn more about our people, projects, and application tips.

At Viridien, your contribution has a real impact on the success of our projects. You’ll work with colleagues from diverse international backgrounds who support one another, share knowledge openly, and welcome new ideas.
From day one, you’ll be paired with a buddy and supported by a dedicated training team. You’ll be mentored by colleagues and managers, with opportunities to develop your technical and professional skills, showcase your work to senior managers, and present at monthly tech talks.

• Initial 22 days annual leave with future increases, complemented by a flexible buying and selling holiday program & bank holiday swap
• Housing allowance of £1200/month for the first six months subject to tax and national insurance and distance relocating.
• Hybrid model and flexible working with up to 2 days at home
• Company pension with generous employer contribution
• Wellbeing Unmind app – puts you in control of your mental health
• Flexible benefits platform with discount schemes including gym membership
• Cycle purchase scheme
• Tailored private medical and dental care
Our Hiring Process

We are also dedicated to ensuring that our hiring process accessible to all. If you require any reasonable adjustments to fully participate in the application or interview stages, please don’t hesitate to contact your recruiter directly.
We see things differently. Diversity fuels our innovation, we value the unique ways in which we differ, and we are committed to equal employment opportunities for all professionals.

Role Overview:
At Huntsman, we are currently looking for a Senior Ecotoxicologist to support our Global EHS Division. In this role, you will provide expert advice across Huntsman businesses by applying your professional judgement in ecotoxicology, exposure science and regulatory compliance. You will support the development and registration of Huntsman products by using hazard and exposure data to conduct environmental risk assessments, support evaluation and authorization processes, and ensure our products remain compliant with global regulatory requirements.
This position is open in multiple European locations: United Kingdom, France, Netherlands Switzerland and Germany. Remote work is an option, and due to the global scope of the role, travel of up to 20% may be required.
Do you think you’re the right fit for this opportunity? Apply today!
Role Responsibilities:
As a Senior Ecotoxicologist, you will:
•
Support Huntsman divisions with environmental hazard and risk assessment expertise across all stages of product development, including R&D of new chemicals, products, markets and uses.
•
Apply knowledge of global regulatory requirements, including TSCA, REACH, Canada, Korea and China, and collaborate with regulatory specialists to ensure compliance.
•
Monitor external ecotoxicology and environmental fate studies, ensuring the appropriate laboratory selection in line with internal and external guidelines.
•
Use in silico tools such as QSAR and read-across for screening, prioritization and, where appropriate, regulatory endpoint data submission.
•
Prepare and support dossier submissions in IUCLID and other relevant formats, including read-across approaches for environmental fate and ecotoxicity endpoint data requirements.
•
Act as the technical lead for ecotoxicology-related issue management, substance defense and advocacy strategies with regulatory bodies.
•
Maintain expertise in ecotoxicology, environmental fate and risk assessment, keeping up to date with relevant regulations, legislation and emerging environmental hazard issues.
•
Represent Huntsman in industry consortia and trade associations, actively participating in meetings and sharing relevant insights with internal stakeholders.
Experience and Competencies:
Minimum Qualifications
•
Advanced degree, Master or PhD, with 10 years of relevant professional experience, preferably in an international company in the chemical or pharmaceutical sector, or at a contract research organization.
•
Extensive applied experience in regulatory ecotoxicology, risk assessment and defense of self-classification and labelling under GHS and CLP.
•
Knowledge of ecotoxicological and environmental fate methods and guidelines, as well as the use of in silico tools, QSARs and read-across.
•
Extensive experience with EU REACH, TSCA and Canada chemical registration.
•
Practical experience with relevant software tools such as OECD QSAR Toolbox, IUCLID, CHESAR and easyTRA.
•
Experience with consortia and trade association work.
•
Fluency in English. Ability to work with colleagues globally in a multicultural environment and in a hybrid setting is essential.
Preferred Qualifications
•
Experience managing teams of scientists.
•
Professional certification as an ecotoxicologist or environmental scientist is a plus.
•
Practical experience with China and Korea chemical registration is a plus.
•
Previous environmental laboratory experience on environmental safety assays is desirable.

Job Title
Senior Scientist – Gene Editing (Bioprocessing R&D)
Location(s)
Cambridge (UK)
About Us
Revvity is a developer and provider of end-to-end solutions designed to help scientists, researchers, and clinicians solve the world’s greatest health challenges. We pair the enthusiasm of an industry disruptor with the experience of a longtime leader. Our team of 11,000+ colleagues from around the globe are vital to our success and the reason we’re able to push boundaries in pursuit of better human health.
Find your future at Revvity
Revvity's Bioprocessing department is at the forefront of developing advanced expression platforms to enable the manufacturing of next-generation biotherapeutics. We offer a diverse portfolio of mammalian host cell lines and innovative expression technologies designed for rapid identification of high-expressing recombinant clones. Leveraging extensive expertise in gene editing and cell line engineering, we deliver custom solutions tailored to our clients' unique manufacturing needs, for both protein and viral vector therapeutics.
Job Summary
As a Senior Scientist in the Bioprocessing R&D team, you will be primarily responsible for executing gene editing projects in mammalian bioproduction cell lines on behalf of clients, applying your expertise to design and implement targeted knockout (KO) and knock-in (KI) strategies. Working to defined project timelines and client requirements, you will bring strong technical independence and a delivery-focused mindset to ensure high-quality outcomes.
In addition to gene editing, you may also contribute to cell line development projects supporting the generation of expressing mammalian cell lines, broadening the scope of your impact within the team.
This is a hands-on, lab-based role suited to a scientist who thrives in a client-project environment, is comfortable working independently to deadlines, and brings a rigorous and methodical approach to experimental design and execution.
Key Responsibilities
• Design and execute gene editing strategies for KO and KI applications in mammalian bioproduction cell lines, planning and troubleshooting experiments to deliver high-quality, reproducible outcomes within agreed project timelines.
• Independently manage assigned project workstreams, ensuring timely delivery and maintaining clear communication with internal project teams.
• Analyse and interpret experimental data, drawing well-reasoned conclusions and proposing appropriate next steps.
• Maintain accurate and up-to-date laboratory records, including laboratory notebooks and relevant technical documentation such as SOPs and experimental reports.
• Communicate scientific results clearly and concisely in internal project meetings and written reports.
• Collaborate effectively with colleagues across the Bioprocessing team and wider organisation to support project delivery.
• Where required, contribute to cell line development activities supporting the generation of expressing mammalian cell lines for client projects.
Essential Competencies & Requirements
• MSc with PhD or equivalent experience in a relevant scientific discipline (Life Sciences, Biochemical Engineering, or closely related field).
• Demonstrated, hands-on expertise in gene editing with a strong track record of designing and executing KO and KI strategies in mammalian cell lines.
• Solid molecular biology skills, including proficiency in cloning techniques (e.g., Gibson Assembly, Golden Gate Assembly), PCR, qPCR, and ddPCR.
• Proven ability to work independently, manage priorities effectively, and deliver results within defined project timelines.
• Strong experimental design and data analysis skills
• Highly organised, detail-oriented, and committed to producing reliable, reproducible scientific results.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present data clearly to internal stakeholders.
• Collaborative team player with a proactive and solution-focused approach.
Desirable Competencies & Requirements
• Experience in CHO cell line development and/or generation of expressing recombinant cell lines (stable pools and/or clones).
• Prior experience working in a client-facing or service-oriented research environment.
• Experience working in GLP or cGMP environments or a strong quality mindset aligned to regulated processes.

- Act as a visible and approachable presence in the community, patrolling designated areas to provide guidance to the public while enforcing road traffic regulations, including the issuance of Penalty Charge Notices when appropriate.
- Support the reduction of traffic congestion and improvement of air quality by managing kerbside activity and ensuring compliance with parking restrictions, using a moped, bicycle, or on foot in all weather conditions.
- Deliver excellent customer service by always engaging respectfully with the public and help to uphold a safe, orderly, and customer-focused environment.
Job Description:
- Monitor on-street and off-street parking areas using a moped, bicycle, or on foot, ensuring vehicles are parked in accordance with relevant regulations, and issue Penalty Charge Notices (PCNs) where non-compliance is identified, in line with local traffic orders.
- Act as a visible and reassuring presence to encourage compliance, promoting responsible parking through positive public engagement and providing accurate, helpful advice on parking rules and facilities to residents and visitors.
- Collect and record comprehensive evidence to support the issuance of PCNs, including writing clear and accurate reports, capturing photographic evidence, and maintaining simultaneously notes in official records.
- Identify and authorise the immobilisation or removal of vehicles in line with regulatory guidelines, where necessary to support enforcement operations or ensure public safety.
- Regularly inspect pay and display machines, signage, and car park equipment, reporting faults, vandalism, or maintenance issues promptly to ensure continuous service and public accessibility.
- Observe and report damaged or missing street furniture, unclear road markings, or suspicious vehicles, contributing to the upkeep and safety of the public realm.
- Attend court hearings or tribunal proceedings where required, providing factual witness statements and supporting documentation when a PCN is formally challenged.
- Collaborate with community safety partners such as Police Community Support Officers and local law enforcement, sharing relevant observations to address anti-social behaviour and support wider community safety initiatives.
- Stay informed about changes in legislation, policies, and systems affecting parking enforcement, attending training sessions and continually developing professional knowledge relevant to the role.
- Support the development of colleagues by providing guidance and informal mentoring, sharing knowledge and promoting a culture of continuous improvement and teamwork.
- Carry out any additional duties commensurate with the role and grading, supporting the flexible delivery of service priorities across the team.
- Operate in line with the company’s core values and professional standards, demonstrating integrity, accountability, and respect in all interactions with the public and colleagues, and contributing positively to the reputation of the service.

Job Description:
What you’ll do in this role:
•
Conduct functional assessments which include initial reviews, face-to-face, video or telephone assessments to evaluate how a claimant’s health condition or disability affects them for various types of benefit.
•
Analyse and interpret clinical information and supporting evidence.
•
Write detailed evidence-based reports to support the DWP/DfC in making informed and objective decisions - no treatment or diagnosis required.
•
Use IT systems to support clinical decision-making and report writing.
•
Develop your clinical knowledge and constantly learn about health conditions which are less familiar to you.
What are PIP and WCA?
•
Personal Independence Payment (PIP) is a benefit for people with a long-term health condition or impairment. It is paid to make a contribution to the extra costs that disabled people may face, to help them lead full, active and independent lives.
•
Work Capability Assessment (WCA) is a functional assessment that looks at a range of different activities relating to physical, mental, intellectual and cognitive functions, to help DWP determine a customer's capability for work or work-related activity.

To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
Group/Division
The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The SPTS division provides advanced wafer processing solutions—including etch, deposition and vapor-based technologies—designed for R&D through high-volume production. With a global presence and strong customer support network, SPTS helps manufacturers across industries improve performance, yield and cost-efficiency. It also offers comprehensive service and spare parts through a worldwide network of service centers and qualified local agents.
What You'll Do
In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
Working as part of the Advanced Development team, you will play a leading role in the conception, and hands-on development of next-generation plasma process technologies that address both current and future semiconductor manufacturing challenges.
You will be expected to proactively define innovative hardware and process solutions, and lead complex development activities spanning plasma etch, deposition, and advanced process integration. The role requires a deep understanding of plasma-surface interactions, hardware-process interactions, and semiconductor device requirements to create differentiated technology solutions for future KLA products.
Key Responsibilities
Technology Development & Innovation
• Lead the development of breakthrough plasma etch and deposition technologies for Advanced Packaging, Photonics, Compound Semiconductor, Quantum, MEMS, and Specialty Semiconductor applications.
• Solve challenging process and hardware problems where solutions are not immediately apparent, applying a combination of first-principles understanding, simulation, experimental design, and data-driven analysis
• Drive invention activities and contribute to patent generation and intellectual property strategy.
Hardware & Process Leadership
• Lead investigation and resolution of complex process integration, plasma physics, equipment, and hardware performance challenges.
• Guide junior engineers and scientists, sharing technical expertise and best practices.
• Lead technical reviews and influence development priorities across the wider organization
• Work closely with engineering teams to influence chamber design, RF systems, gas delivery, thermal management, endpoint control, and process diagnostics.
Simulation & Modelling
• Interpret modelling tools such as COMSOL or equivalent simulation packages to predict plasma behaviour, materials interactions, process performance, and hardware design impacts.
• Develop physical models and mechanistic understanding to guide future technology directions.
Customer and Partner Engagement
• Collaborate with customers, research institutes, universities, and strategic development partners to understand future technology requirements.
• Act as a technical representative for KLA in customer reviews, consortium activities, technical conferences, and collaborative research programmes.
• Present complex technical findings to internal leadership and external stakeholders.
Data Analysis & Reporting
• Generate clear technical reports, publications, invention disclosures, and executive-level summaries.
• Communicate complex technical concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.
This position will involve international travel to meet with customers, attend conferences/collaborative work and occasional shift work is expected.
Occasional domestic and international travel, including to the United States, may be required as part of this role
KLA, is proud to be an inclusive and diverse employer.
What we will offer you?
Our benefits package includes:
Annual leave starting at 25 days (plus bank holidays), contributory pension scheme, cash health plan, cycle to work scheme, global bonus plan, share scheme, rewards scheme, life assurance, generous shift allowance and overtime premiums.
Minimum Qualifications
• PhD in Physics, Plasma Physics, Chemistry, Materials Science, Semiconductor Technology, Electronic Engineering, or a related discipline.
• Significant industrial or research experience in plasma processing, semiconductor equipment development, or advanced semiconductor manufacturing.
• Strong understanding of plasma etch and/or deposition technologies.
• Knowledge of RF power delivery systems, plasma sources, thermal management, vacuum systems, endpoint detection, and semiconductor equipment architecture
About KLA
We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.

At KLA, our interviews seek to understand your individual skills, problem-solving approach and authentic thinking. To ensure a fair and consistent evaluation, the use of AI, recording tools or other technologies to generate, suggest or provide responses during interviews—whether virtual or in person—is not permitted unless explicitly approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation or invited by the interviewer. KLA is committed to advancing innovation through responsible AI, and we value candidates who share this mindset.

At Expedia Group, we help travelers explore the world, one journey at a time. As a global travel company powered by passionate people, trusted partnerships, and leading technology, we connect travelers, partners, and advertisers through our consumer brands, B2B network, and travel advertising business.

sanger.wd103.myworkdayjobs.com/wellcomes.description_excerpt:
Do you want to help us improve human health and understand life on Earth? Make your mark by shaping the future to enable or deliver life-changing science to solve some of humanity’s greatest challenges.
We are seeking a highly motivated and creative Postdoctoral Fellow or Senior Postdoctoral Fellow to join the Martin group at the Wellcome Sanger Institute, to develop and apply statistical and machine learning methods to cell-free DNA from pregnant women and people.
About the group:
The Martin group works on the genetic basis of rare and common disease, using large-scale human genetic datasets with rich linkage to electronic health records and questionnaires. Over the last few years, we have had a particular emphasis on the genetics of neurodevelopmental disorders and related traits, the genetics of complex disease in populations with high levels of consanguinity, and factors influencing germline mutation rates.
The group is now opening new research directions involving genomics and multi-omics in very early life. Most conditions in the earliest stages of life remain untouched by large-scale genomics, and molecular predictors that could guide clinical management are urgently needed. We are building a programme spanning a clinical continuum from pregnancy loss, through fetal growth restriction, to complications of premature birth. This includes large-scale sequencing of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from pregnant women and people to identify monogenic causes of pregnancy loss and identify biomarkers for fetal growth restriction, as well as genetic and multi-omic studies of neonatal conditions using nationwide dried blood spots.
What you'll be doing:
This particular role is focused on cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from pregnant women and people. cfDNA in maternal plasma is a mixture of maternal and fetal (placental) molecules, and offers a route to studying fetal genomes and placental biology at a scale that is impossible with fetal tissue. Possible projects include:
• Developing new statistical and deep learning methods for calling fetal and maternal genotypes from high-coverage sequence data on cfDNA, and for discovering new Mendelian disease genes using the resulting data. These methods will then be applied to study pregnancy complications in large samples.
• Developing biomarkers for pregnancy complications from methylation-aware wholegenome sequence data on cfDNA, including methods development to incorporate both epigenetic and genetic information in the same assay. You will have the opportunity to collaborate with groups at the Norwegian Institute of Public Health (Siri Eldevik Håberg), the University of Helsinki (Simone Rubinacci) and elsewhere.
About you:
We are recruiting at two levels: Postdoctoral Fellow and Senior Postdoctoral Fellow. In both cases, you will have a demonstrable background in statistics or statistical genetics. Experience of working with cfDNA is highly desirable but not essential. The role would particularly suit if you have previously worked on methods for somatic variant calling, or for phasing and imputation from low-coverage sequence data.You would also bring excellent software development skills, since the methods developed here are intended to be applied across several large cohorts and shared with collaborators. The Senior Postdoctoral Fellow role is intended for someone with particularly strong experience in these areas who is ready to work with a high degree of independence, to shape the direction of the methods development, to lead collaborations and to mentor more junior members of the group. You will be considered at the level that best matches your experience, so please apply even if you are unsure which position fits. Prospective candidates are welcome to contact Hilary Martin (hcm@sanger.ac.uk) with informal queries before deciding whether to apply.
Essential Skills:
• PhD in a relevant area (statistics, statistical genetics, genetics, genomics, bioinformatics, machine learning or similar)
• Strong background in statistics or statistical genetics, including the ability to develop, implement and benchmark new statistical methods
• Experience working with raw sequence data (alignments, variant calling, quality control)
• Experience analysing large-scale human genetic or genomic data
• Full working proficiency in Python and/or R, and Unix/Linux
• Experience or enthusiasm for using AI tools to improving productivity in scientific research, statistical methods development and/or software development
• Knowledge and understanding of statistical methods appropriate for large-scale genetic research
• Previous experience writing highly reproducible code with github, Snakemake/Nextflow, RMarkdown or similar
• Experience developing pipelines or software for large-scale analyses of genomic data, including running workflows efficiently on HPC and/or cloud infrastructure
• Creativity and original scientific ideas
• Enthusiasm and commitment
• Attention to detail
• Effective problem-solving skills
• Ability to communicate ideas and results effectively both verbally and in writing
• Ability to prioritise, work independently and organise own workload
• Ability to collaborate effectively with an interdisciplinary team and collaborators
Senior Postdoctoral Fellow as above, with the following additional skills:
• Completion of a previous postdoctoral position, or other highly relevant training or experience
• Experience of developing methods for variant calling from sequence data, or for phasing and imputation from low-coverage sequence data
• Evidence of substantial research contributions and intellectual leadership, demonstrated through publications, methods, software or other relevant outputs, appropriate to career stage and opportunities.
• Specialist knowledge and understanding to drive the project from the outset
• Demonstrated ability to lead collaborations and to supervise or mentor junior researchers
You will join our supportive and collaborative Postdoctoral Fellow community, with access to training, learning and networking across the Institute.
Other information:
For further details, please see role profile for Postdoctoral Fellow and Senior Postdoctoral Fellow.

For Senior Postdoctoral Fellow (dependent upon skills and experience): £44,305-£49,893

Condé Nast is one of the world's most renowned media publishing companies, creating and distributing every type of media today, spanning print and digital publishing in all formats. Job Description
Location:
London, GB
Condé Nast is one of the world’s most renowned media companies creating and distributing every type of media today – print, video and film, digital, audio and social.  Our company is home to iconic brands including Vogue, The New Yorker, GQ, Glamour, AD, Vanity Fair and Wired, among many others. The company's award-winning content reaches 84 million consumers in print, 367 million in digital and 379 million across social platforms, and generates more than 1 billion video views each month. We are seeking a Vice President of Communications to lead our communications in the UK, a market essential to our global brand presence.
Based in London, this person will shape how Condé Nast, its brands and its leaders show up across the British media and cultural landscape. The remit spans the full breadth of the business: from Condé Nast’s commercial strategy and corporate reputation to the journalism, editors, talent and cultural moments behind brands including Vogue, GQ, WIRED, Condé Nast Traveller, Glamour, Tatler, House & Garden and The World of Interiors.
This is both a U.K. leadership role and a senior position within Condé Nast’s global communications team. The VP will lead the U.K. communications team, advise senior executives and editorial leaders, and work closely with communications colleagues around the world on issues and opportunities that increasingly cross markets.
Condé Nast thrives on collaboration, and our teams come together in the office four days a week (Monday - Thursday).
We value diversity of background, views and cultures. We celebrate people for their personal qualities, skills and contributions, recognising the power our brands have to influence and shape culture.
The leadership role reports to the Global Communications Officer and the position is based in London.
Key Responsibilities
• Own Condé Nast’s communications strategy and reputation in the U.K., with a clear point of view on where the company and its brands should be part of the conversation.
• Lead corporate, business and brand communications across Condé Nast’s U.K. portfolio, spanning commercial priorities, editorial initiatives, talent, launches, partnerships and major cultural moments.
• Lead and develop the U.K. communications team, setting priorities and creating ambitious, high-quality work across a complex portfolio of brands.
• Serve as a senior member of the global communications team, working closely with the Chief Communications Officer and senior communications leadership on company-wide priorities and issues.
• Advise and position senior U.K. and European leaders on media strategy, messaging, speaking opportunities and reputation.
• Advise editorial leaders how to achieve maximum impact and external awareness for their work. Implement plans to do so.
• Build communications around Condé Nast’s journalism and editorial leadership, identifying where our editors, writers and creative talent can shape conversations beyond our own platforms.
• Bring a deep understanding of the British news, business, media, technology and cultural landscape, spotting opportunities early and knowing when Condé Nast should lead a conversation, join one or stay out of it.
• Maintain strong relationships with influential journalists and editors across national, business, trade, broadcast and cultural media.
• Lead communications through sensitive and high-profile issues, providing clear counsel to senior leaders and coordinating responses across functions and markets.
• Work closely with editorial, commercial, consumer marketing, people and other teams to turn business priorities into compelling external narratives.
• Write and oversee sharp, high-quality communications materials, from messaging and executive briefs to announcements, Q&As and statements.
• Help shape how Condé Nast communicates globally, bringing ideas, judgment and lessons from the U.K. market to the wider communications organisation.
What we’re looking for
• A senior communications leader with significant experience in media, publishing, entertainment or another business where brands, talent, culture and corporate reputation intersect.
• A problem-solver that tries new approaches and unexpected ideas.
• Deep knowledge of the U.K. media landscape and strong, current relationships with the journalists and editors who shape business, media and cultural conversations.
• The ability to move comfortably between corporate reputation and brand storytelling, and to understand how the two reinforce each other.
• Excellent news judgment and a strong instinct for what makes a story, rather than simply what makes an announcement.
• A sophisticated understanding of how media consumption, platforms and influence are changing, particularly in the U.K., and what that means for modern communications.
• A track record of advising senior executives and high-profile talent, including in complex or sensitive situations.
• Significant crisis and issues-management experience, with the judgment to operate calmly and decisively when the stakes are high.
• Experience leading and developing high-performing communications teams.
• The ability to operate effectively across a global organization, building strong relationships across markets, brands and functions.
• Exceptional writing and editing skills, with the ability to make complicated ideas clear, concise and compelling.
• Approximately 12+ years of relevant communications experience. We are more interested in the depth and quality of that experience than where you acquired it.
• Demonstrated ability to lead teams through uncertainty and change, providing a steady and confident hand during business transformation.
• Proven experience in managing enterprise-level accountability, ensuring communications strategy is seamlessly aligned with broader business objectives and cultural values.
What benefits do we offer?
• 25 days holiday (plus bank holidays) and extra days of annual leave if you move house or want to volunteer.
• You’ll have access to a competitive pension scheme, Bupa Private Healthcare, Season ticket loans…

The Senior Quantitative Risk Actuary is a key member of the 2nd line risk management function, responsible for delivering quantitative oversight across the validation, reserving, financial market and credit risk, and broader capital and risk assessment processes. The role is central to maintaining regulatory compliance, supporting the ORSA, and ensuring robust model governance aligned to Solvency II and Lloyd’s standards. The position requires a qualified actuary with  experience in model validation and reserve risk assessment, and the ability to provide effective independent challenge across Capital Modelling, Reserving, Finance, and Risk stakeholders.
Main Duties
The role encompasses a broad range of risk management activities and as Senior Quantitative Risk Actuary your duties will include:
Internal Model Validation & Reporting
• Lead the end‑to‑end Internal Model validation process for S1084 and S1176, ensuring methodology, assumptions, governance and documentation meet Solvency II and Lloyd’s requirements.
• Support the Independent Actuarial Qualified Person in providing independent assurance over adequacy and effectiveness of the internal model validation framework and process
• Produce the annual Validation Reports, articulating findings, limitations, and model improvements, and presenting these to risk and model governance Committees.
Reserving Risk Oversight
• Provide 2nd Line oversight of reserving processes, including review of assumptions, methodologies, uncertainty analyses, and reserve risk capital outputs.
• Perform independent reviews on key drivers such as inflation, claims emergence patterns, social/economic trends, and operational influences.
• Challenge the Reserving Committee outputs, reserve movements, and the modelling of reserve distributions.
Financial Market & Credit Risk Oversight
• Conduct independent assessment of market risk exposures, investment strategies, sensitivity analyses, and the appropriateness of methodologies used by 1st Line functions.
• Oversight of credit risk reviews covering reinsurance counterparties, broker credit, investment credit exposures, concentrations, and stress impacts.
• Provide quantitative challenge to capital charges, risk appetite metrics, and control effectiveness across market and credit risks.
Stress & Scenario Testing / ORSA Support
• Develop, review, and challenge quantitative stress and scenario tests for the ORSA and independent validation, including macroeconomic, geopolitical, reserve‑related and market‑related stresses.
• Collaborate with Risk, Underwriting, Capital Modelling and Finance to ensure scenarios are severe but plausible, aligned to Lloyd’s expectations, and cover emerging risks.
• Produce ORSA inputs and analytical commentary to support forward‑looking capital and solvency assessments.
Model Risk Management
• Develop the 2nd Line model risk framework.
• Review and challenge 1st line testing of models
Ad‑hoc Quantitative Risk Assessments
• Support business plan and strategy assessments through quantitative analysis such as scenario testing. Considering emerging risks and risk profile changes.
• Support investigations into risk events, near misses, or unexpected model behaviours with quantitative analysis and challenge.
Stakeholder Engagement & Governance
• Present quantitative findings to Risk & Capital Committees, Reserving Committee and other governance forums.
• Build relationships across Capital Modelling, Reserving, Finance, Underwriting, and senior management to provide clear, credible and evidence‑based challenge.
• Support broader Risk Management initiatives including framework enhancements, policy updates, and regulatory requests.
Regulatory responsibilities
• Support in the production of Regulatory Reports (Validation, ORSA and adhoc requirements)
Our requirements
Relevant experience
Essential
• Fully qualified actuary (e.g., FIA or equivalent) with post‑qualification experience.
• Internal Model Validation experience within a Lloyd’s or Solvency II‑regulated insurer.
• Technical understanding of reserve risk, including methodologies, assumptions, inflation analysis, and uncertainty.
• Hands‑on experience reviewing and challenging capital model components (parameterisation, dependency structures, model change, model outputs).
• Good understanding of insurance to enable effective engagement at all levels within the business
• Good working knowledge of financial market risk and credit risk methodologies, including capital charges and stress/sensitivity analysis.
• Involvement in ORSA processes, including stress and scenario testing.
• Advanced analytical and critical thinking skills
• Ability to communicate complex quantitative outputs clearly to senior stakeholders and governance committees.
Desirable
• Experience working in a 2nd Line oversight role within the Lloyd’s market.
• Good understanding of Enterprise Risk Management methodologies
• Exposure to model governance frameworks, model risk taxonomies, and documentation standards.
• Exposure to internal models through build, maintenance and /or validation
• Understanding of investment strategy, ALM considerations, or credit portfolio analytics.
• Experience designing or improving SST frameworks, emerging risk quantification, or strategic/business plan scenario analysis.
• Prior involvement in regulatory interactions (Lloyd’s, PRA, CBI).
• Familiarity with underwriting risk modelling concepts and capital attribution.
• Experience presenting findings at committees such as RCC, Reserving Committee or Board‑level forums
Personal Skills
• Experience in preparing and presenting high quality reports for internal and external stakeholders demonstrating attention to detail.
• Exceptional interpersonal skills. This is a people facing role requiring a professional that can tailor communication style to different stakeholder needs and personalities.
• Ability to manage and prioritise competing demands. Ability to work efficiently in a diverse and dynamic environment.
• Excellent planning and organisational skills.
• Quantitative and analytical skills.
• Able to think critically to solve problems and justify decisions
• Capable of demonstrating judgement and decision making
• The ability to challenge and question established practices and contribute to the development of new processes.
• Self-motivated with a professional outlook
ABOUT US
Chaucer is a leading insurance group at Lloyd’s, the world’s specialist insurance market. We help protect industries around the world from the risks they face. Our customers include major airlines, energy companies, shipping groups, global manufacturers and property groups.
Our headquarters are in London, and we have international offices in Bermuda, Copenhagen, Dubai and Singapore to be closer to our clients across the world. To learn more about us please visit our website.

“CVI Infrared Optics is a part of the IDEX Materials, Science and Solutions (MSS) platform. Since 1982, CVI Infrared Optics has been manufacturing advanced optical components for high performance optronics systems. When you need robust optical components and assembly expertise for your mission critical application, we can provide world-class solutions.“
About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Single Point Diamond Turning (SPDT) Technician to join our Fabrication Team, manufacturing high-precision infrared and visible optical components to exacting customer specifications.
In this role, you will set, operate and optimise ultra-precision diamond turning machinery to produce optical components with exceptional dimensional accuracy and surface finish requirements. Working to micron and sub-micron tolerances, you will manufacture complex optical surfaces while maintaining the highest standards of quality, cleanliness and workmanship.
Working with delicate, high-value optical materials, you will take ownership of components from machine setup and process preparation through to final inspection, ensuring all products meet drawing, process and customer requirements.
Key Responsibilities
• Set, operate and optimise Single Point Diamond Turning machines to manufacture precision optical components.
• Interpret engineering drawings, specifications and manufacturing documentation accurately.
• Manufacture components to micron and sub-micron dimensional tolerances and optical surface quality requirements.
• Select and install appropriate tooling, fixtures and machine parameters for production activities.
• Verify machine setup, tooling condition and process parameters prior to manufacture.
• Produce first-off components and conduct in-process inspections to ensure process conformity.
• Monitor machine performance and make appropriate process adjustments to maintain quality and repeatability.
• Inspect finished components using precision metrology and measurement equipment.
• Carry out optical surface inspections in accordance with applicable standards and customer requirements.
• Identify defects, contamination, handling damage, scratches, chips or other non-conformances and escalate where required.
• Clean components using approved methods while maintaining strict optical cleanliness standards.
• Complete process sheets, inspection records and production documentation accurately.
• Maintain full traceability throughout the manufacturing process.
• Follow Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), work instructions and approved manufacturing processes.
• Understand and support Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) activities to ensure equipment reliability and performance.
• Maintain a clean, organised and controlled working environment appropriate for precision optical manufacturing.
• Handle delicate and high-value optical materials and components with care throughout manufacture and inspection.
• Work effectively both independently and as part of a wider fabrication team.
• Prioritise workload effectively to meet production schedules and customer delivery requirements.
• Identify and support opportunities to improve manufacturing efficiency, quality, yield and repeatability.
• Support Continuous Improvement and Lean Manufacturing initiatives.
• Report equipment issues, tooling concerns, quality issues and process abnormalities promptly.
• Comply with all company Health & Safety, Quality and Environmental procedures.
Key Relationships
• Work closely with colleagues within the Fabrication Department to share knowledge, skills and best practice.
• Maintain regular communication with your Supervisor, raising concerns or issues promptly.
• Build positive working relationships across the business through a professional, respectful and collaborative approach.
Working Environment
This role is based within a precision optical fabrication environment where components are often small, delicate and high value. The successful candidate will be comfortable working within a controlled manufacturing environment and maintaining consistently high standards of cleanliness, accuracy and housekeeping.
Due to the nature of the products, strict adherence to documented manufacturing processes, careful handling of components and excellent attention to detail are essential.
Physical Requirements
The role involves supporting the day-to-day operation of the fabrication area, including moving optical components, tooling and materials between departments. Regular lifting of items in excess of 5kg may be required.
Reasonable adjustments may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the role.
Essential Skills & Experience
• Proven experience setting and operating Single Point Diamond Turning (SPDT) machinery or CNC Lathe equipment.
• Experience manufacturing precision components to micron and sub-micron tolerances.
• Experience achieving demanding optical surface finish requirements.
• Ability to read and accurately interpret engineering drawings and technical specifications.
• Experience using precision metrology and inspection equipment.
• Good understanding of ultra-precision machining principles and process control.
• Experience working with controlled manufacturing documentation, SOPs and process sheets.
• Understanding of Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) principles and preventative maintenance requirements.
• High level of manual dexterity and hand-eye coordination.
• Excellent attention to detail and quality standards.
• Ability to work accurately with small, delicate and high-value optical components.
• Strong organisational and time-management skills.
• Ability to work independently and take ownership of work quality.
• Strong team-working skills.
• Commitment to quality, accuracy and right-first-time manufacturing.
• Good understanding of Health & Safety requirements within a manufacturing environment.
Desirable Skills & Experience
• Experience machining infrared optical materials including Germanium, Silicon and Multispectral Zinc Sulphide (MSZnS).
• Previous experience within optical manufacturing or ultra-precision engineering environments.
• Experience manufacturing freeform or aspheric optical components.
• Experience using interferometers, profilometers or advanced optical metrology equipment.
• Experience working to ISO and DIN optical standards.

About the role:
Reports to Head of Enterprise Architecture
At Aztec Group we credit our technology as one of the core ingredients to our award-winning outsourced solutions. We are currently looking for an Enterprise Data Architect to join our architecture team and help Aztec to deliver their exciting new technology strategy, leveraging Databricks.
This role will centre on the design, implementation and maintenance of data models and related architecture for our Azure Data Platform. You will provide technical expertise under the direction of an experienced Manager and with support for continuing professional development, the ideal candidate will become a key part of the Group’s Architecture team.
Key responsibilities:
•
Define and maintain the enterprise data architecture, including target-state designs, roadmaps, and architectural standards and patterns.
•
Own the architecture of our Databricks Lakehouse platform, including workspace design, Unity Catalog structure, medallion architecture, and environment strategy.
•
Design and govern integration patterns for sharing data with external clients and third parties, including secure, scalable approaches using Databricks Delta Sharing, APIs, and file-based exchange where appropriate.
•
Lead the design and adoption of Master Data Management (MDM), including entity definitions, golden-record strategy, match-and-merge rules, and stewardship processes.
•
Establish standards and practices for optimising Databricks performance and cost — cluster and compute strategy, Delta table, caching, and workload right-sizing.
•
Define data modelling standards (conceptual, logical, physical) across analytical and operational domains.
•
Work with data governance colleagues to embed data quality, lineage, cataloguing, classification, and access-control policies into platform design.
•
Ensure architectures meet security, privacy, and regulatory requirements, including GDPR and data residency considerations.
•
Review solution designs, provide architectural assurance, and support engineering teams through design authority and peer review.
•
Design data architectures that enable AI adoption — ensuring data is discoverable, well-governed, and AI-ready for machine learning, GenAI, and agentic use cases across the business.
•
Partner with AI/ML teams to define patterns for feature engineering, model data pipelines, vector search, and the safe exposure of enterprise data to AI systems.
•
Evaluate emerging technologies and make pragmatic build/buy/adopt recommendations, including data and AI enablement opportunities.
Skills, knowledge and expertise:
•
Deep, hands-on proficiency with Databricks, including Unity Catalog, Delta Lake, workflows, and platform administration concepts.
•
Practical experience with Databricks Delta Sharing and designing integration patterns for external data sharing (e.g. Delta Sharing, secure APIs, event streaming, managed file transfer), including the security and contractual considerations involved.
•
Strong track record designing and implementing Master Data Management solutions, including tooling selection, data stewardship models, and reference data management.
•
Demonstrable expertise in Databricks performance and cost optimisation at scale.
•
Strong data modelling skills (dimensional, 3NF, Data Vault or similar) and experience defining enterprise data models.
•
Solid grounding in Azure, including storage, networking, and identity concepts relevant to data platforms.
•
Experience with data governance frameworks and tools (e.g. Microsoft Purview), data quality management, metadata, and lineage tooling.
•
Strong SQL and working knowledge of Python and/or Spark.
•
Understanding of data security and privacy: encryption, access control (RBAC/ABAC), data masking, and regulatory compliance (GDPR).
•
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain architectural decisions in plain language to executive and non-technical audiences.
We will provide the training, both in house for relevant technical knowledge and also professional qualifications to enhance your professional development. You will need to be quick to learn new systems and business processes and great with people, as close working relationships between our colleagues and clients is at the heart of what we do.

Significant exposure to non-performing and re-performing loan (NPL/RPL) securitizations and whole loan portfolios within private structures
•
Emphasis on loan-level and cashflow modelling across illiquid mortgage credit, including collateral analysis, recovery assumptions and structural waterfalls

Minimum of 3 years of relevant professional experience at a top sell-side or buy-side institution in a front office quantitative role

Exceptional quant / analytical skills – knowledge of advanced pricing techniques (Monte Carlo, prepayment modelling and scenario engines), asset pricing theory, probability theory, and cash flow / bond maths (e.g. OAS calculations)

Experience designing, coding, and implementing pricing and surveillance frameworks for automation / streamlining of tasks
•
Strong coding skills in Python – candidates for whom Python experience is limited to occasional / hobby usage should not apply

Familiar with statistical coding packages and modelling in SAS, R or Python

Working knowledge of Linux/Unix/Bash and SQL would be a plus.

Footwear Technologist
Reporting to Head of Footwear, the Footwear Technologist will ensure timely delivery of assigned footwear ranges, guaranteeing that styles meet technical, quality and safety specifications and are fit for purpose. The role supports the Technical Manager in maintaining departmental quality standards, collaborates with design and buying to develop a commercially viable range, and leads supplier technical activities to achieve the brand’s fit, performance and cost targets.
Key responsibilities
Review & research
•
Conduct seasonal block and last reviews in collaboration with buying and design teams.
•
Maintain and update the footwear specification library (lasts, patterns, sole specifications, material cards) using customer feedback and market benchmarking.
•
Analyse market trends, competitor footwear construction and material innovations to inform style and performance improvements.
•
Review competitor footwear to maintain an innovative, profitable and on‑trend range while protecting fit integrity.
Product development & quality assurance
•
Manage end‑to‑end footwear development from concept through proto, fit, pre‑production and production sign‑off, ensuring consistency in construction and commercial viability.
•
Produce clear, timely tech packs for footwear (last references, lasted patterns, uppers, insocks, midsoles, outsoles, heel units, box/pack specs).
•
Provide accurate fit comments at fittings (upper fit, toe room, last shape, heel counter) and secure gold seals on schedule.
•
Identify technical risks at sign‑off (lasting, sole bonding, stitchline tolerances, heel attachment) and work with buyers/suppliers to mitigate.
•
Specify and monitor footwear testing requirements (flex tests, abrasion, slip resistance, sole bond strength, water resistance, ageing/colourfastness) and interpret results to guide corrective actions.
•
Maintain product testing and compliance records and coordinate with internal/external labs.
•
Liaise with overseas QA teams to maintain brand expectations through training and factory audits focused on lasting, sole attachment, injection.
Strategy & supplier management
•
Lead root‑cause analysis for footwear returns (delamination, outsole separation, stitch failure, poor lasting) and develop corrective action plans with suppliers to reduce recurrence.
•
Support sourcing decisions for lasts, sole manufacturers, midsole suppliers and material mills to balance quality, cost and continuity.
•
Conduct factory technical process audits (lasting lines, cementing, molding, vulcanizing, stitchdown) and recommend process improvements.
•
Build and maintain strong relationships with footwear suppliers, last makers and sole houses; ensure suppliers are aware of technical, legal and ethical requirements.
Range planning & build
•
Work closely with buying and merchandising to ensure styles are prototyped, fitted and sealed per the critical path.
•
Ensure suppliers comply with customer technical specifications and corporate ethical/technical audit standards to avoid critical path delays.
•
Confirm all active suppliers meet technical standards and that necessary audits, process qualifications and tooling approvals are in place.
•
Maintain accurate grading rules, size conversion tables and pack/box specifications to prevent production inconsistencies.
Leadership & people management
•
Line manage and motivate technical team members where applicable; provide clear communication, coaching and development.
•
Conduct performance reviews, objective setting and regular one‑to‑ones.
•
Champion continuous improvement and adoption of relevant footwear technologies or CAD tools.
•
Act as a role model for company culture and lead by example on quality, safety and commercial accountability.
Qualifications & experience
•
Bachelor’s degree in Footwear Technology, Footwear Design, Materials Science, Product Technology or a related discipline preferred.
•
Minimum 3 years’ footwear technical experience (development, production and supplier management) — experience with offshore footwear suppliers is essential.
•
Demonstrable product knowledge across a wide range of footwear constructions (cemented, lasted, vulcanized, molded, injection/direct attach, welted).
•
Experience in value retail or multi‑product footwear environments is advantageous.
•
Proven track record in issuing timely fit comments, securing gold seals and managing customer feedback/returns.
Skills & competencies
•
Deep understanding of footwear construction, lasts, patternmaking for uppers, insole/midsole/outsole engineering and materials (leather, suede, synthetics, knitted uppers, EVA/PU midsoles, rubber/TPU outsoles).
•
Familiarity with PLM/ERP systems.
•
Strong knowledge of footwear testing methods and relevant industry standards (e.g., SATRA/ASTM/EN ISO guidance) and ability to interpret requirements for commercial compliance.
•
Excellent verbal and written communication and stakeholder management skills across design, buying, suppliers and QA teams.
•
Effective time management, organisation and ability to work under pressure to meet critical path deadlines.
•
Strong analytical, problem‑solving and negotiation skills with commercial awareness and focus on cost‑effective solutions.
•
Proficient in MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook).
Other
•
Willingness to travel overseas regularly to supplier factories for technical audits, fittings and development meetings.
•
Commitment to ethical sourcing, product safety and continuous improvement.
This role requires a dedicated professional who balances footwear technical expertise, supplier management and leadership to deliver high‑quality, commercially successful footwear products.

At Dalcour Maclaren, we're key players in the Utilities and Infrastructure industry, bringing the UK and Ireland closer to Net Zero every day. Our land, environmental and geospatial experts work together to unlock the consents needed by our clients to deliver key projects. Our services include land access and assembly, agricultural liaison, planning, environmental impact assessments and geospatial mapping. Join us, and play your part in helping us to achieve our vision; to be the professional services team of choice, leading the Utilities and Infrastructure industry to a sustainable future.
What is our Placement Surveyor programme?
Our Placement Surveying programme is a 12-month programme designed to give you a comprehensive exposure to surveying within Utilities & Infrastructure. Through working on live projects, learning from industry experts and networking opportunities, we will help you to building your technical and professional skills needed for a career and to make the valuable contributions towards your academic fulfilments for your degree.
What will you get up to? What does the job involve?
In a nutshell, our Placement Surveyors will be working on utilities and infrastructure projects helping to manage land-related issues during the development of infrastructure like pipelines, power lines, or roads. Their role includes negotiating access agreements, assessing and handling compensation claims for landowners, ensuring compliance with regulations, and minimising the impact of projects on agricultural land and rural properties. You will act as the valuable intermediary between our clients and landowners, overseeing effective land access and management while ensuring fair compensation and resolving disputes.
A day in the life of a Placement Surveyor is highly varied and could involve any of the following:
•
Providing expertise: supporting with the delivery of land and property advice to a range of clients, helping them to make informed decisions.
•
Heads of terms and licences: assisting with Heads of terms and contractual agreements with stakeholders on behalf of clients to aid the delivery of infrastructure projects.
•
Site noticing: getting out and about with your colleagues putting up notices to inform land owners of client schemes.
•
Records of condition: helping the team to review and advise on various different land types, undertaking schedules of condition of private land.
•
Site visits: witnessing the tangible impact your work is having on Utilities & Infrastructure throughout the UK by seeing the projects in-person and monitoring their progress.
•
Compensation and valuation: assessing the financial impact of infrastructure projects, agreeing compensation claims; think valuation of land and property, agricultural losses, and general disturbance.
•
Handling landlord and tenant relationships: supporting with tenancy agreements and ensuring legal compliance.
•
Problem solving: working with the wider DM team and your clients to problem solve, advise on risks and reach solutions.
•
Data and technology: delivering large scale schemes through innovative big data, technology and reporting functions
What do we need from you?
We don’t expect you to be an expert from day one, we're seeking the right combination of skills and attributes, like proactivity, problem-solving and a keen eye for detail that will contribute to your success.
However, to successfully enroll on our programme, you will need to hold a RICS accredited or relevant degree plus a full UK driving licence and your own means of transport will also be essential.

As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions.

Join Northern Trust's Enterprise Chief Operating Office (ECOO) and play a critical role in shaping compensation strategies that support one of the organization's most dynamic and globally connected functions. As a Compensation Senior Consultant, you will serve as a trusted advisor to business leaders and HR partners, helping drive compensation decisions that attract, retain, and motivate top talent while supporting business objectives. This role combines deep compensation expertise with strong consulting, analytical, and influencing skills to provide market-informed, equitable, and governance-aligned solutions across a range of complex talent and organizational matters. You will partner closely with leaders to translate compensation philosophy into practical business outcomes, guide critical pay decisions, and deliver insights that support effective workforce and talent strategies.
Key Responsibilities
• Serve as a trusted compensation advisor for assigned business units and functions within ECOO, providing guidance to HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, and business leaders on complex compensation matters.
• Develop recommendations for internal moves, retention situations, off-cycle adjustments, reorganizations, and other pay decisions, balancing external market data, internal equity, business priorities, affordability, and governance requirements.
• Translate business and workforce needs into practical compensation solutions across base pay, short-term incentives, sales or other variable compensation programs, and recognition programs, as applicable.
• Conduct and present job evaluations, leveling assessments, market-pricing analyses, and pay recommendations; support the consistent application of the global job architecture, career framework, and salary structures.
• Facilitate compensation discussions with HR and business leaders, explain complex or sensitive information clearly, challenge assumptions constructively, and build alignment around recommended actions.
• Monitor external compensation practices, labor market developments, and relevant regulatory changes; assess implications and recommend appropriate responses.
• Develop executive-ready analyses and materials that convert complex compensation data into clear findings, alternatives, risks, and recommendations.
• Lead and support the global annual compensation cycle, including planning, data validation, market and pay-equity analysis, system testing, stakeholder communications, manager and HR enablement, issue resolution, and post-cycle review.
Knowledge and Skills
Advanced knowledge of broad-based compensation principles and practices, including:
• Market pricing and compensation surveys
• Job evaluation, job leveling, and job architecture
• Salary structures and pay administration
• Base pay, merit, and variable or incentive compensation
• Internal equity, pay equity, pay transparency, and compensation governance
In addition, the successful candidate will possess:
• Strong compensation consulting and stakeholder management skills, with the judgment to develop, explain, and defend recommendations.
• Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills; able to work with complex data, identify material themes and risks, develop alternatives, and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
• Demonstrated business acumen and ability to connect compensation decisions to talent, workforce, financial, risk, and business considerations.
• Strong written, verbal, presentation, and facilitation skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with HR partners, managers, and senior leaders.
• Strong project management and change management capabilities, including the ability to organize work across multiple stakeholders, priorities, countries, and workstreams.
• Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills, with proficiency working with large datasets, analytical models, and executive-ready presentations.
Experience
• 7+ years of progressive compensation experience, preferably within the financial services industry.
Education
• Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Human Resources, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Work Authorization
Applicants must have the right to work in the United Kingdom at the time of application and for the duration of employment.
Please note that Northern Trust is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role. This includes Skilled Worker visas, Global Business Mobility routes, Graduate visas, Youth Mobility Scheme, High Potential Individual visas, Scale-up Worker visas, Temporary Worker visas, and other employer-sponsored visa categories.
Working with Us
As a Northern Trust partner, you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture, which has a strong history of financial strength and stability. Movement within the organization is encouraged, senior leaders are accessible, and you can take pride in working for a company committed to an inclusive workplace and assisting the communities we serve.
Philanthropy is deeply rooted in Northern Trust’s history and is an essential element of our culture. Employees around the world give their time and talent to work for the greater good of their communities.
Reasonable Accommodation
Northern Trust is committed to working with and providing adjustments to individuals with health conditions and disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please email our HR Service Center at MyHRHelp@ntrs.com, or alternatively you can discuss your individual requirements with the recruiter you are working with.
